### Emoji in `[brackets]`

-   `[any emoji]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the repository
-   `[number]` Connects multiple places that are related to each other across the file
-   `[🧠]` Marks a place where there is something to decide and think about.
-   `[🕕]` List of models _(that should be progresively updated)_
    -   Prompt: Update available models and their prices, search online
-   `[🔼]` Marks an entity (function, class, type,...) in other project (like Promptbook.studio) which should be moved to this repository
-   `[🚉]` Marks an types / interfaces / structures fully serializable as JSON, not marking `string_` and `number_` prefixed aliases
-   `[🧹]` Need to implement garbage collection
-   `[🐣]` Easter eggs
-   `[💩]` Shitty code that needs refactoring
-   `$` When entity (function, class) starts by `$`, it means it is not pure and can have side effects.
-   3x `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed before releasing a pre-release version.
-   4x (and more) `!` Marks a place that needs to be fixed as soon as possible.
-   `@@@` Marks a place where text / documentation / ... must be written.
-   [⚫] Code in this file should never be published in any package
-   [🟢] Code in this file should never be published into packages that could be imported into browser environment
-   [🔵] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/browser`
-   [🟡] Code in this file should never be published outside of `@promptbook/cli`
-   [💞] Ignore a discrepancy between file name and entity name

### Dictionary

-   **Promptbook Engine vs. Agent Server** sre two distinct parts you should know the difference:
    -   **Promptbook Engine** is the core engine that powers AI agents, it is located in `/src` folder. It is framework-agnostic and can be used in different applications. It can run as standalone javascript/typescript library, CLI environment, or be integrated into different applications. It can be also runned in Agent Server:
    -   **Agent Server** is a specific application that uses the Promptbook Engine to provide a web and API interface for creating and interacting with AI agents. It is located in `/apps/agents-server` folder.
-   **Commitments** are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents
    -   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, etc.
    -   Commitments are in the folder `/src/commitments`
    -   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g., `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a begining of the line and end by new co
    -   Agent source with commitments is parsed by two functions:
        -   `parseAgentSource` which is a lightweight parser for agent source, it parses basic information and its purpose is to be quick and synchronous. The commitments there are hardcoded.
        -   `createAgentModelRequirements` which is an asynchronous function that creates model requirements it applies each commitment one by one and works asynchronously.

#### Agents server installed on VPS _(as additional context)_

-   There are two distinct things:
    1. Entire VPS
    2. Each server
-   On one VPS there can be multiple servers and each server has its own domain
-   Most things (like agents, projects, metadata, etc.) are living on each server and some things (like environment variables, superadmin, etc.) are bound to entire VPS
-   Purpose of this is to be able to run multiple clients on one VPS and each client can have its own server with its own domain and settings
-   The entire VPS is managed by superadmin and each server is managed by normal admin of that server _(or superadmin can also manage each server)_
-   Superadmin has always name `admin` and password hardcoded in environment variable `ADMIN_PASSWORD`
-   The VPS is installed by running [the `install.sh`](install.sh) script on a fresh VPS
-   Servers can be added and removed by superadmin on `/superadmin/servers` page

#### The Agents Server menu _(as additional context)_

The menu of the agent server looks like this:

1. The navigation hierarchy
    - Icon and Server name _(for example Promptbook Agents Server)_
    - arrow ">" and Agents or picked agent name (organized in folders)
    - arrow ">" and the view Profile / Chat / Book of the agent or nothing if no agent is picked
2. The menu items
    - Documentation
    - System
3. Control panel and user menu
    - Control panel
    - User menu with the avatar and the name of the user

#### Database migrations for Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   Migrations are located in `apps/agents-server/src/database/migrations`
-   Be aware that table names in migrations have prefix `prefix_` _(look at existing migrations for reference)_
-   Migrations should be backwards compatible:
    -   Meaning that earlier versions of the server should be able to run with the database after migration without any issues.
    -   This is important because we want to have the same database for production and preview environments.
    -   This database will be migrated to the latest version of the preview environment, but the production environment should be able to run with it without any issues.
    -   The only thing that can happen is that older versions of the server will not be able to use new features.
    -   Adding new columns, tables, etc. is fine, but do not remove or rename existing ones, and do not change the meaning of existing columns or tables.
    -   When in doubt, prefer to add new things instead of changing existing ones.

#### Metadata of Agents server _(as additional context)_

-   There is a table called `Metadata`.
-   It has `key` and `value` fields.
-   It is a similar concept to configuration, but this configuration can be changed by administrators in the Agents Server website.

#### Book Language blueprint _(as additional context)_

Book language is a domain-specific language used for defining AI agents in the Promptbook Engine and Agents server.
It has lightweight syntax and keywords (the commitments) that allow you to define the "soul" of the agent.
The book language is designed to be human-readable and easy to write, while also being powerful enough to express complex agent behaviors.

Every agent has its source defined in the book language, which is called "agent source". The agent source is parsed and processed by the Promptbook Engine to create the actual AI agent that can interact with users and perform tasks.
This agent source is internally converted to a structured format called "agent model requirements" which are the actual raw technical instructions for the AI model to run the agent.

There is a standalone book language documentation on each agent server on `/api/docs/book.md` route, for example `https://live.ptbk.io/api/docs/book-language.md?language=en`.
Use it as a reference for the syntax and semantics of the book language, and modify `apps/agents-server/src/utils/bookLanguageDocumentation/createStandaloneBookLanguageMarkdown.ts` if it is relevant to the change you are doing.

##### Commitments _(as additional context and part of Book Language)_

Commitments are basic syntax elements that add specific functionalities to AI agents written in `book` language.

-   They are used in `agentSource`, there are commitments like `PERSONA`, `RULE`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE CALENDAR`, `USE PROJECT`, `META IMAGE`, `CLOSED`, etc.
-   They are in the folder `src/commitments`.
-   Each commitment starts with a keyword, e.g. `PERSONA`, `KNOWLEDGE`, `USE PROJECT`, etc. on a beginning of the line and ends by a new commitment or the end of the book.
-   There is a general pattern that the commitment keyword is followed by a space and then by the content of the commitment, for example:
    -   `PERSONA You are a helpful assistant that helps with cooking recipes.`
    -   `USE MCP https://mcp.example.com/server`
-   In the commitment context, you can reference external agents, for example:
    -   `TEAM You can talk to {Criminal lawyer} and {Financial advisor}`

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01R39HmrxxTQc9UeNLKdyiXa","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t[^] by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n2\t\n3\t[✨🚓] when generating a system message, do not duplicate instructions\n4\t\n5\tFor example, when there is a commitment `WRITING RULES`, this section should be in the generated system message only once:\n6\t\n7\t```\n8\t### Writing rules\n9\tThese instructions apply only to how you write: tone, formatting, length, emoji usage, punctuation, and similar presentation choices.\n10\tThey do not change your task-solving behavior, business logic, or factual decision-making rules.\n11\tIf multiple writing-rules blocks conflict, prefer the newer writing-rules blocks.\n12\tIf a writing rule conflicts with a writing sample, follow the explicit writing rule while keeping the writing sample as the primary voice exemplar.\n13\t\n14\t```\n15\t\n16\t-   This pattern is relevant for all commitments, not only for `WRITING RULES`\n17\t-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.\n18\t-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.\n19\t-   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bff3bbec-f916-44e2-9b1b-3a9effb2c4a0","uuid":"afa8a60a-627a-41dc-84fe-de2a073565b8","timestamp":"2026-09-14T18:01:53.010Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/hejny/work/promptbook/prompts/2026-09-0270-writing-rules-instructions-duplicates.md","content":"[^] by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `max` - Implementation in progress\n\n[✨🚓] when generating a system message, do not duplicate instructions\n\nFor example, when there is a commitment `WRITING RULES`, this section should be in the generated system message only once:\n\n```\n### Writing rules\nThese instructions apply only to how you write: tone, formatting, length, emoji usage, punctuation, and similar presentation choices.\nThey do not change your task-solving behavior, business logic, or factual decision-making rules.\nIf multiple writing-rules blocks conflict, prefer the newer writing-rules blocks.\nIf a writing rule conflicts with a writing sample, follow the explicit writing rule while keeping the writing sample as the primary voice exemplar.\n\n```\n\n-   This pattern is relevant for all commitments, not only for `WRITING RULES`\n-   Keep in mind the DRY _(don't repeat yourself)_ principle.\n-   Do a proper analysis of the current functionality before you start implementing.\n-   Add the changes into the [changelog](changelog/_current-preversion.md)","numLines":19,"startLine":1,"totalLines":19}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01G4joMS2RKESsLEVYge21Gv","type":"tool_result","content":"1\timport { spaceTrim } from 'spacetrim';\n2\timport type { AgentModelRequirements } from '../../book-2.0/agent-source/AgentModelRequirements';\n3\timport { createWritingRulesSection } from '../_common/createWritingCommitmentSections';\n4\timport { BaseCommitmentDefinition } from '../_base/BaseCommitmentDefinition';\n5\t\n6\t/**\n7\t * `WRITING RULES` commitment definition.\n8\t *\n9\t * The `WRITING RULES`/`WRITING RULE` commitment adds constraints that apply strictly to writing style\n10\t * and presentation rather than task-solving behavior.\n11\t *\n12\t * Example usage in agent source:\n13\t *\n14\t * ```book\n15\t * WRITING RULES Keep every response under 120 words\n16\t * WRITING RULE Always end the message with an emoji\n17\t * ```\n18\t *\n19\t * @private [🪔] Maybe export the commitments through some package\n20\t */\n21\texport class WritingRulesCommitmentDefinition extends BaseCommitmentDefinition<'WRITING RULES' | 'WRITING RULE'> {\n22\t    public constructor(type: 'WRITING RULES' | 'WRITING RULE' = 'WRITING RULES') {\n23\t        super(type);\n24\t    }\n25\t\n26\t    /**\n27\t     * Short one-line description of `WRITING RULES`/`WRITING RULE`.\n28\t     */\n29\t    public get description(): string {\n30\t        return 'Add writing-only constraints such as tone, length, formatting, or emoji usage.';\n31\t    }\n32\t\n33\t    /**\n34\t     * Icon for `WRITING RULES`/`WRITING RULE`.\n35\t     */\n36\t    public get icon(): string {\n37\t        return '📝';\n38\t    }\n39\t\n40\t    /**\n41\t     * Markdown documentation for `WRITING RULES`/`WRITING RULE` commitment.\n42\t     */\n43\t    public get documentation(): string {\n44\t        return spaceTrim(`\n45\t            # ${this.type}\n46\t\n47\t            Adds instructions that apply strictly to how the agent writes.\n48\t\n49\t            ## Key aspects\n50\t\n51\t            - All writing rules are treated equally regardless of singular/plural form.\n52\t            - Use it for writing-only constraints such as tone, formatting, length, emoji usage, punctuation, or reading level.\n53\t            - Do **not** use it for problem-solving behavior, policy, tool usage, or decision-making logic. type { BookCommitment } from '../../../commitments/_base/BookCommitment';\nimport type { ParsedCommitment } from '../../../commitments/_base/ParsedCommitment';\nimport { getCommitmentDefinition } from '../../../commitments/_common/getCommitmentDefinition';\nimport type { chococake } from '../../../utils/organization/really_any';\nimport type { AgentModelRequirements } from '../AgentModelRequirements';\nimport type { CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions } from '../CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions';\nimport { parseTeamCommitmentContent } from '../parseTeamCommitment';\nimport type { TeammateProfile } from '../TeammateProfileResolver';\n\n/**\n * Commitment types whose content may contain compact agent references that must be resolved before applying the commitment.\n *\n * @private internal constant of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nconst COMMITMENTS_WITH_AGENT_REFERENCES = new Set<BookCommitment>(['FROM', 'IMPORT', 'IMPORTS', 'TEAM']);\n\n/**\n * Applies parsed commitments one by one while keeping the per-commitment steps focused and easy to follow.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param commitments - Commitments already filtered for DELETE-like invalidations.\n * @param options - Optional reference and teammate resolvers.\n * @returns Requirements after all applicable commitments are processed.\n *\n * @private function of `createAgentModelRequirementsWithCommitments`\n */\nexport async function applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    commitments: ReadonlyArray<ParsedCommitment>,\n    options?: CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions,\n): Promise<AgentModelRequirements> {\n    for (const [index, commitment] of commitments.entries()) {\n        if (shouldSkipCommitmentApplication(commitment, index, commitments.length)) {\n            continue;\n        }\n\n        const commitmentContent = await resolveCommitmentContent(commitment, options?.agentReferenceResolver);\n        requirements = await preResolveTeammateProfilesForTeamCommitment(\n            requirements,\n            commitment,\n            commitmentContent,\n            options,\n        );\n        requirements = applyCommitmentDefinitionSafely(requirements, commitment, commitmentContent);\n    }\n\n    return requirements;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolves compact agent references for commitment types that support them.\n *\n * @param commitment - Commitment currently being applied.\n * @param agentReferenceResolver - Optional resolver for compact agent references.\n * @returns Original or resolved commitment content.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nasync function resolveCommitmentContent(\n    commitment: ParsedCommitment,\n    agentReferenceResolver?: CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions['agentReferenceResolver'],\n): Promise<string> {\n    if (!agentReferenceResolver || !isAgentReferenceCommitment(commitment.type)) {\n        return commitment.content;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        return await agentReferenceResolver.resolveCommitmentContent(commitment.type, commitment.content);\n    } catch (error) {\n        console.warn(\n            `Failed to resolve commitment references for ${commitment.type}, falling back to safe defaults:`,\n            error,\n        );\n        return getSafeReferenceCommitmentFallback(commitment.type, commitment.content);\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Returns a safe fallback content when a resolver fails to transform a reference commitment.\n *\n * @param commitmentType - Commitment being resolved.\n * @param originalContent - Original unresolved commitment content.\n * @returns Fallback content that keeps requirement creation resilient.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nfunction getSafeReferenceCommitmentFallback(commitmentType: BookCommitment, originalContent: string): string {\n    if (commitmentType === 'FROM') {\n        return 'VOID';\n    }\n\n    if (commitmentType === 'IMPORT' || commitmentType === 'IMPORTS' || commitmentType === 'TEAM') {\n        return '';\n    }\n\n    return originalContent;\n}\n\n/**\n * Checks whether the commitment content may need agent-reference resolution before application.\n *\n * @param commitmentType - Commitment type to check.\n * @returns `true` when the commitment can contain compact agent references.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `resolveCommitmentContent`\n */\nfunction isAgentReferenceCommitment(commitmentType: ParsedCommitment['type']): boolean {\n    return COMMITMENTS_WITH_AGENT_REFERENCES.has(commitmentType);\n}\n\n/**\n * Determines whether a commitment should be skipped before resolution or application.\n *\n * @param commitment - Commitment under consideration.\n * @param commitmentIndex - Zero-based position among filtered commitments.\n * @param commitmentCount - Total number of filtered commitments.\n * @returns `true` when the commitment should not be applied.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nfunction shouldSkipCommitmentApplication(\n    commitment: ParsedCommitment,\n    commitmentIndex: number,\n    commitmentCount: number,\n): boolean {\n    return commitment.type === 'CLOSED' && commitmentIndex !== commitmentCount - 1;\n}\n\n/**\n * Pre-resolves teammate profiles for TEAM commitments so the TEAM commitment definition can reuse richer metadata.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param commitment - Commitment currently being prepared.\n * @param commitmentContent - Already resolved TEAM commitment content.\n * @param options - Optional teammate profile resolvers.\n * @returns Requirements with pre-resolved teammate profiles stored in metadata when possible.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nasync function preResolveTeammateProfilesForTeamCommitment(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    commitment: ParsedCommitment,\n    commitmentContent: string,\n    options?: CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions,\n): Promise<AgentModelRequirements> {\n    const profileResolver = options?.teammateProfileResolver ?? options?.agentReferenceResolver;\n    if (commitment.type !== 'TEAM' || !profileResolver?.resolveTeammateProfile) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        const parsedTeammates = parseTeamCommitmentContent(commitmentContent, { strict: false });\n        const preResolvedTeammateProfiles = clonePreResolvedTeammateProfiles(requirements._metadata);\n\n        for (const teammate of parsedTeammates) {\n            if (preResolvedTeammateProfiles[teammate.url]) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            const profile = await profileResolver.resolveTeammateProfile(teammate.url);\n            if (profile) {\n                preResolvedTeammateProfiles[teammate.url] = profile;\n            }\n        }\n\n        return {\n            ...requirements,\n            _metadata: {\n                ...requirements._metadata,\n                preResolvedTeammateProfiles,\n            },\n        };\n    } catch (error) {\n        console.warn('Failed to pre-resolve teammate profiles for TEAM commitment:', error);\n        return requirements;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Clones the metadata bucket used to cache teammate profiles resolved ahead of TEAM commitment application.\n *\n * @param metadata - Current requirements metadata.\n * @returns Mutable copy of the cached teammate profile map.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `preResolveTeammateProfilesForTeamCommitment`\n */\nfunction clonePreResolvedTeammateProfiles(metadata?: Record<string, chococake>): Record<string, TeammateProfile> {\n    return {\n        ...((metadata?.preResolvedTeammateProfiles as Record<string, TeammateProfile> | undefined) ?? {}),\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Applies the registered commitment definition while isolating the failure handling from the main loop.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param commitment - Commitment whose definition should be applied.\n * @param commitmentContent - Final content passed into the definition.\n * @returns Updated requirements, or the original requirements when the commitment fails.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `applyCommitmentsToAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nfunction applyCommitmentDefinitionSafely(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    commitment: ParsedCommitment,\n    commitmentContent: string,\n): AgentModelRequirements {\n    const definition = getCommitmentDefinition(commitment.type);\n    if (!definition) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    try {\n        return definition.applyToAgentModelRequirements(requirements, commitmentContent);\n    } catch (error) {\n        console.warn(`Failed to apply commitment ${commitment.type}:`, error);\n        return requirements;\n    }\n}\n","numLines":220,"startLine":1,"totalLines":220}}}

haystack.split(needle).length - 1;\n17\t}\n18\t\n19\tdescribe('createAgentModelRequirements commitment aggregation', () => {\n20\t    it('keeps multi-PERSONA content merged without duplication or reordering', async () => {\n21\t        const agentSource = validateBook(\n22\t            spaceTrim(`\n23\t            Persona Agent\n24\t            PERSONA First persona trait.\n25\t expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'Second persona trait.')).toBe(1);\n34\t        expect(requirements.systemMessage.indexOf('First persona trait.')).toBeLessThan(\n35\t { spaceTrim } from 'spacetrim';\nimport { describe, expect, it } from '@jest/globals';\nimport { createAgentModelRequirements } from './createAgentModelRequirements';\nimport { validateBook } from './string_book';\n\n/**\n * Counts literal substring occurrences inside a string.\n *\n * @param haystack - Full text to scan.\n * @param needle - Exact substring to count.\n * @returns Number of literal matches.\n *\n * @private test utility of `createAgentModelRequirements.commitmentAggregation.test.ts`\n */\nfunction countOccurrences(haystack: string, needle: string): number {\n    return haystack.split(needle).length - 1;\n}\n\ndescribe('createAgentModelRequirements commitment aggregation', () => {\n    it('keeps multi-PERSONA content merged without duplication or reordering', async () => {\n        const agentSource = validateBook(\n            spaceTrim(`\n            Persona Agent\n            PERSONA First persona trait.\n            PERSONA Second persona trait.\n        `),\n        );\n\n        const requirements = await createAgentModelRequirements(agentSource);\n\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'You are Persona Agent')).toBe(1);\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'First persona trait.')).toBe(1);\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'Second persona trait.')).toBe(1);\n        expect(requirements.systemMessage.indexOf('First persona trait.')).toBeLessThan(\n            requirements.systemMessage.indexOf('Second persona trait.'),\n        );\n    });\n\n    it('keeps only the last GOAL commitment effective after rewrite ordering', async () => {\n        const agentSource = validateBook(\n            spaceTrim(`\n            Goal Agent\n            GOAL Inherited goal.\n            RULE Stay concise.\n            GOALS Final goal.\n        `),\n        );\n\n        const requirements = await createAgentModelRequirements(agentSource);\n\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'Inherited goal.')).toBe(0);\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.systemMessage, 'Final goal.')).toBe(1);\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.promptSuffix, 'Inherited goal.')).toBe(0);\n        expect(countOccurrences(requirements.promptSuffix, 'Final goal.')).toBe(1);\n        expect(requirements.systemMessage).toContain('## Rules');\n        expect(requirements.systemMessage).toContain('-   Stay concise.');\n    });\n});\n","numLines":59,"startLine":1,"totalLines":59}}}

URL or local path declared in an IMPORT commitment.\n * @returns Imported text ready to append to the system message.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `importReferencedFiles`\n */\nasync function createImportedFileSystemMessage(fileUrl: string): Promise<string> {\n    await mockedSecurityCheck(fileUrl);\n\n    const { content, mimeType } = await readImportedFile(fileUrl);\n    if (isBinaryMimeType(mimeType)) {\n        throw new Error(`Importing binary files is not allowed: ${mimeType}`);\n    }\n\n    const plugin = $fileImportPlugins.find((fileImportPlugin) => fileImportPlugin.canImport(mimeType));\n    if (!plugin) {\n        throw new Error(`No import plugin found for MIME type: ${mimeType}`);\n    }\n\n    return plugin.import(content, mimeType);\n}\n\n/**\n * Reads one imported file and normalizes the MIME type expected by file import plugins.\n *\n * @param fileUrl - Remote URL or local path declared in an IMPORT commitment.\n * @returns Plain-text content together with a normalized MIME type.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `createImportedFileSystemMessage`\n */\nasync function readImportedFile(fileUrl: string): Promise<{ content: string; mimeType: string }> {\n    if (isValidUrl(fileUrl)) {\n        const response = await promptbookFetch(fileUrl);\n        if (!response.ok) {\n            throw new Error(`Failed to fetch ${fileUrl}: ${response.statusText}`);\n        }\n\n        return {\n            content: await response.text(),\n            mimeType: normalizeImportedMimeType(response.headers.get('Content-Type')),\n        };\n    }\n\n    /*\n    TODO: !!!! Commented out this case because we need to work in Browser-compatible mode in many packages, use passed `fs` instead\n    } else if (isValidFilePath(fileUrl)) {\n        // [x🟢x] This code is expected to run in Node environment if local files are used\n        const fs = await import('fs/promises');\n        content = await fs.readFile(fileUrl, 'utf-8');\n        const extension = getFileExtension(fileUrl);\n        mimeType = extensionToMimeType(extension as string);\n    */\n\n    throw new Error(`Invalid file URL or path: ${fileUrl}`);\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalizes MIME types returned by fetch so plugin lookup works on bare MIME values without charset suffixes.\n *\n * @param mimeType - Raw response MIME type header.\n * @returns Normalized MIME type fallbacking to `text/plain`.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `readImportedFile`\n */\nfunction normalizeImportedMimeType(mimeType: string | null): string {\n    return (mimeType || 'text/plain').split(';')[0]!.trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * Appends extracted MCP server identifiers from the original source.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param agentSource - Original agent source used for MCP extraction.\n * @returns Requirements with `mcpServers` set when MCP commitments are present.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `augmentAgentModelRequirementsFromSource`\n */\nfunction appendMcpServers(requirements: AgentModelRequirements, agentSource: string_book): AgentModelRequirements {\n    const mcpServers = extractMcpServers(agentSource);\n    if (mcpServers.length === 0) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    return {\n        ...requirements,\n        mcpServers,\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Appends non-commitment prose from the source after filtering out blank lines and markdown horizontal rules.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source including non-commitment lines.\n * @returns Requirements with the remaining prose appended to the system message.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `augmentAgentModelRequirementsFromSource`\n */\nfunction appendNonCommitmentContent(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments,\n): AgentModelRequirements {\n    const nonCommitmentContent = getNonCommitmentContent(parseResult);\n    if (!nonCommitmentContent) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    return appendSystemMessageSection(requirements, nonCommitmentContent);\n}\n\n/**\n * Appends unknown commitment blocks as final extra context without applying commitment side effects.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source including unknown commitment blocks.\n * @returns Requirements with unknown commitment context appended at the end of the system message.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `augmentAgentModelRequirementsFromSource`\n */\nfunction appendUnknownCommitmentContent(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments,\n): AgentModelRequirements {\n    const unknownCommitmentContent = getUnknownCommitmentContent(parseResult);\n    if (!unknownCommitmentContent) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    return appendSystemMessageSection(requirements, unknownCommitmentContent);\n}\n\n/**\n * Joins unknown commitment blocks into their final extra-context representation.\n *\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source including unknown commitment blocks.\n * @returns Unknown commitment source blocks in their original order.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `appendUnknownCommitmentContent`\n */\nfunction getUnknownCommitmentContent(parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments): string {\n    return parseResult.unknownCommitments\n        .map((commitment) => commitment.source)\n        .filter(Boolean)\n        .join('\\n\\n');\n}\n\n/**\n * Collects plain-text lines that were not parsed as commitments and should still become part of the final system message.\n *\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source including non-commitment lines.\n * @returns Joined non-commitment content or an empty string when there is nothing to append.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `appendNonCommitmentContent`\n */\nfunction getNonCommitmentContent(parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments): string {\n    return parseResult.nonCommitmentLines\n        .filter((line, index) => index > 0 || !parseResult.agentName)\n        .filter((line) => line.trim())\n        .filter((line) => !isHorizontalLine(line))\n        .join('\\n')\n        .trim();\n}\n\n/**\n * Checks whether a line is a markdown horizontal separator.\n *\n * @param line - Source line to inspect.\n * @returns `true` when the line is a thematic break.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `getNonCommitmentContent`\n */\nfunction isHorizontalLine(line: string): boolean {\n    return HORIZONTAL_LINE_PATTERN.test(line);\n}\n\n/**\n * Appends example interactions assembled from INITIAL MESSAGE and USER/AGENT sample commitments.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source used to recover initial message content.\n * @returns Requirements with the example interaction block appended when examples exist.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `augmentAgentModelRequirementsFromSource`\n */\nfunction appendExampleInteractions(\n    requirements: AgentModelRequirements,\n    parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments,\n): AgentModelRequirements {\n    const exampleInteractionsContent = createExampleInteractionsContent(parseResult, requirements.samples);\n    if (!exampleInteractionsContent) {\n        return requirements;\n    }\n\n    return appendSystemMessageSection(requirements, exampleInteractionsContent);\n}\n\n/**\n * Creates the formatted example-interaction section appended to the final system message.\n *\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source used to recover the initial message commitment.\n * @param samples - Parsed USER/AGENT sample pairs already stored on requirements.\n * @returns Formatted example interaction block or `null` when no examples exist.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `appendExampleInteractions`\n */\nfunction createExampleInteractionsContent(\n    parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments,\n    samples: AgentModelRequirements['samples'],\n): string | null {\n    const examples = collectExampleInteractionLines(parseResult, samples);\n    if (examples.length === 0) {\n        return null;\n    }\n\n    return spaceTrim(\n        (block) => `\n            ## Sample of communication with the agent:\n\n            ${block(examples.join('\\n\\n'))}\n        `,\n    );\n}\n\n/**\n * Collects the individual lines used in the example interaction section.\n *\n * @param parseResult - Parsed source used to recover the initial message commitment.\n * @param samples - Parsed USER/AGENT sample pairs already stored on requirements.\n * @returns Individual example interaction snippets in output order.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `createExampleInteractionsContent`\n */\nfunction collectExampleInteractionLines(\n    parseResult: ParsedAgentSourceWithCommitments,\n    samples: AgentModelRequirements['samples'],\n): string[] {\n    const examples: string[] = [];\n    const initialMessage = parseResult.commitments.find((commitment) => commitment.type === 'INITIAL MESSAGE')?.content;\n\n    if (initialMessage) {\n        examples.push(\n            spaceTrim(\n                (block) => `\n                    **Agent:**\n                    ${block(initialMessage)}\n                `,\n            ),\n        );\n    }\n\n    if (samples && samples.length > 0) {\n        for (const sample of samples) {\n            examples.push(\n                spaceTrim(\n                    (block) => `\n                        **User:** ${block(String(sample.question))}\n\n                        **Agent:**\n                        ${block(sample.answer)}\n                    `,\n                ),\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    return examples;\n}\n\n/**\n * Appends a single system-message section using the same blank-line separation used throughout the original implementation.\n *\n * @param requirements - Current requirements snapshot.\n * @param section - Section content to append.\n * @returns Requirements with the additional system-message block appended.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `augmentAgentModelRequirementsFromSource`\n */\nfunction appendSystemMessageSection(requirements: AgentModelRequirements, section: string): AgentModelRequirements {\n    return {\n        ...requirements,\n        systemMessage: spaceTrim(\n            (block) => `\n                ${block(requirements.systemMessage)}\n\n                ${block(section)}\n            `,\n        ),\n    };\n}\n\n/**\n * Mocked security check for imported files.\n *\n * @param urlOrPath - The URL or local path of the file to check.\n * @returns A promise that resolves if the file is considered safe.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `createImportedFileSystemMessage`\n */\nasync function mockedSecurityCheck(urlOrPath: string): Promise<void> {\n    // TODO: Implement proper security checks\n    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10));\n\n    if (urlOrPath.includes('malicious')) {\n        throw new Error(`Security check failed for: ${urlOrPath}`);\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Checks whether the given MIME type belongs to a binary file.\n *\n * @param mimeType - The MIME type to check.\n * @returns `true` when the MIME type is treated as binary.\n *\n * @private internal utility of `createImportedFileSystemMessage`\n */\nfunction isBinaryMimeType(mimeType: string): boolean {\n    return BINARY_MIME_TYPE_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => mimeType.startsWith(prefix));\n}\n","numLines":400,"startLine":1,"totalLines":400}}}

type { string_book } from './string_book';\n\n/**\n * Creates model requirements for an agent based on its source.\n *\n * There are 2 similar functions:\n * - `parseAgentSource` which is a `@promptbook/core`\n */\nexport async function createAgentModelRequirements(\n    agentSource: string_book,\n    modelName?: string_model_name,\n    availableModels?: readonly AvailableModel[],\n    llmTools?: LlmExecutionTools,\n    options?: CreateAgentModelRequirementsOptions,\n): Promise<AgentModelRequirements> {\n    // If availableModels are provided and no specific modelName is given,\n    // use preparePersona to select the best model\n    if (availableModels && !modelName && llmTools) {\n        const selectedModelName = await selectBestModelUsingPersona(agentSource, llmTools);\n        return createAgentModelRequirementsWithCommitments(agentSource, selectedModelName, options);\n    }\n\n    // Use the new commitment-based system with provided or default model\n    return createAgentModelRequirementsWithCommitments(agentSource, modelName, options);\n}\n\n/**\n * Selects the best model using the preparePersona function\n * This directly uses preparePersona to ensure DRY principle\n *\n * @param agentSource The agent source to derive effective profile text from\n * @param llmTools LLM tools for preparing persona\n * @returns The name of the best selected model\n *\n * @private function of `createAgentModelRequirements`\n */\nasync function selectBestModelUsingPersona(\n    agentSource: string_book,\n    llmTools: LlmExecutionTools,\n): Promise<string_model_name> {\n    // Parse agent source to get the effective profile description\n    const { agentName, personaDescription } = parseAgentSource(agentSource);\n\n    // Use agent name as fallback if no profile description is available\n    const description = personaDescription || agentName || 'AI Agent';\n\n    try {\n        // Use preparePersona directly\n        const { modelsRequirements } = await preparePersona(description, { llm: llmTools }, { isVerbose: false });\n\n        // Extract the first model name from the requirements\n        if (modelsRequirements.length > 0 && modelsRequirements[0]?.modelName) {\n            return modelsRequirements[0].modelName;\n        }\n\n        // Fallback: get available models and return the first CHAT model\n        const llmTools.listModels();\n        const chatModels = availableModels.filter(({ modelVariant }) => modelVariant === 'CHAT');\n\n        if (chatModels.length === 0) {\n            throw new Error('No agent source string that may contain `USE MCP` commitments.\n * @returns Array of MCP server identifiers\n *\n * @private TODO: [🧠] Maybe should be public\n */\nexport function @deprecated Use parseAgentSource instead\n *\n * @private\n */\nexport function extractAgentProfileImage(agentSource: string_book): string_url_image | null {\n    const { meta } = regions.push(createRegion(headingLine, bodyLines));\n        headingLine = line;\n        bodyLines = [];\n    }\n\n    regions.push(createRegion(headingLine, bodyLines));\n\n    return {\n        titleKey: headingLine === null ? null : normalizeSectionTitle(headingLine),\n        headingLine,\n        isBodySeparatedByBlankLine: bodyLines[0] !== undefined && bodyLines[0].trim() ===   Be nice.\n            `),\n        );\n    });\n\n    it('keeps a repeated identical section only once', () => {\n        const systemMessage = spaceTrim(`\n            ## Privacy\n\n            -   Use \\`turn_privacy_on\\` when the user asks for a private conversation.\n            -   Use \\`turn_privacy_on\\` when the user asks for a private conversation.\n                -   Do not claim that end-to-end encryption is implemented yet.\n            `),\n        );\n    });\n\n    it('joins merged list blocks into one compact list', () => {\n        const systemMessage = spaceTrim(`\n            ## Language\n\n            - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013Qu8C22WDZXU9u6MvRaen1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and\n2\t    thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now\n3\t    names the agent which implemented it:\n4\t\n5\t    -   A prompt status line signs its work with the agent in front of the harness, as\n6\t        `` [x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.13 23 minutes ``.\n7\t        The `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status lines and the run trace of the round all report it, and a prompt continued\n8\t        through `--git-changes continue` keeps the agent in each of its chronological `interrupted, continued by …`\n9\t        reports.\n10\t    -   The reported name is the display name of the Book — its `META FULLNAME`, or the plain title on its first line\n11\t        — so `agents/coding/developer.book` signs as its Book title and not as its normalized identifier.\n12\t    -   A run started without `--agent` reports exactly what it reported before.\n13\t\n14\t-   Fixed `MockedChat` typing animations blinking for messages without ids by assigning stable playback-only ids before rendering each simulated transcript.\n15\t\n16\t-   Fixed the rich `ptbk coder run` dashboard so an animated agent avatar can no longer overwrite its own UI in an\n17\t    exact-width terminal pane:\n18\t\n19\t    -   The shared frame layout now leaves one physical terminal column unused, preventing boxed rows from\n20\t        auto-wrapping and keeping incremental cursor-based redraws aligned with their logical frame rows.\n21\t    -   Added a focused VS Code terminal preset and regression coverage for the terminal-width invariant.\n22\t\n23\t-   Added agent-specific prompt routing to `ptbk coder`:\n24\t\n25\t    -   A ready `[ ]` prompt can now target the Book passed in `--agent` with a backtick-delimited path, filename,\n26\t        filename without `.book`, or the Book title from its first line. For example, a run using\n27\t        `--agent agents/coding/developer.book` accepts `agents/coding/developer.book`, `developer.book`,\n28\t        `developer`, and `Promptbook Developer` routing tokens.\n29\t    -   Agent references work alongside the existing model and harness routing tokens, and `ptbk coder list --agent\n30\t        <path.book>` previews the same agent-specific queue without starting a harness.\n31\t    -   Added an Unslopper agent preset next to the developer preset in the local VS Code terminal scripts and\n32\t        documented agent-specific routing on the `ptbk coder` landing page.\n33\t\n34\t-   The help of `ptbk` does not advertise the deprecated commands anymore. `run`, `login`, `make`, `prettify`, `test`,\n35\t    `list-models`, `list-scrapers`, `start-agents-server` and `start-pipelines-server` are all leftovers of the old\n36\t    pipeline system, yet nine of the fifteen commands which `ptbk --help` listed were exactly those, each one with its\n37\t    own `Deprecated:` paragraph, so the listing which is supposed to introduce the CLI was mostly made of commands\n38\t    nobody should start using. `ptbk --help`, and the same listing which plain `ptbk` prints when it asks for a\n39\t    subcommand, now offers only the commands which are meant to be used - `coder`, `agent`, `agent-folder`,\n40\t    `agents-server`, `about` and `hello`. Nothing was removed: every deprecated command still runs, still warns that it\n41\t    is deprecated when it is used, still explains the deprecation in its own help - `ptbk run --help` - and is still\n42\t    reachable through `ptbk help run`. Only the \"did you mean\" hint for a mistyped command stops pointing at them.\n43\t    Being left out of the help is now simply a part of what deprecating a command means, written once in\n44\t    `$deprecateCliCommand`, so any command deprecated later disappears from the help on its own.\n45\t\n46\t-   `ptbk` without a subcommand no longer falls back to the deprecated `ptbk run`. Until now `run` was registered as\n47\t    the default command of the CLI, so everything which did not name a command - `ptbk ./write-cv.book`, a mistyped\n48\t    `ptbk codr` or a stray option - was quietly handed over to the pipeline runner of the old system, which was the\n49\t    last thing a deprecated command should be doing. Plain `ptbk` now asks to specify a subcommand and prints the\n50\t    top-level help, exactly like `ptbk coder`, `ptbk agent`, `ptbk agent-folder` and `ptbk agents-server` already did\n51\t    when they were called without one of their own subcommands, and that one shared behavior is now written once\n52\t    instead of five times. Anything which is not a command is refused with `unknown command` and a \"did you mean\"\n53\t    hint instead of being executed as a pipeline, so a script which still passes a book path to `ptbk` fails loudly\n54\t    rather than appearing to succeed. `ptbk run` itself is untouched and keeps working for everyone who asks for it\n55\t    explicitly. The command list in the help now starts with `coder`, followed by `agent`, `agent-folder` and\n56\t    `agents-server`, and the deprecated commands of the old pipeline system are listed after them.\n57\t\n58\t-   `ptbk coder` now saves the run trace of every prompt round, so a finished run can still be analyzed afterwards.\n59\t    Until now the only durable record of a round was the one status line written into the prompt file: the live\n60\t    runtime log holding everything the harness and the verification command had written was a temporary artifact,"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bff3bbec-f916-44e2-9b1b-3a9effb2c4a0","uuid":"0667d0c2-5155-45fb-bc46-490e1ba68fcf","timestamp":"2026-09-14T18:11:21.348Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/hejny/work/promptbook/changelog/_current-preversion.md","content":"-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and\n    thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now\n    names the agent which implemented it:\n\n    -   A prompt status line signs its work with the agent in front of the harness, as\n        `` [x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.13 23 minutes ``.\n        The `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status lines and the run trace of the round all report it, and a prompt continued\n        through `--git-changes continue` keeps the agent in each of its chronological `interrupted, continued by …`\n        reports.\n    -   The reported name is the display name of the Book — its `META FULLNAME`, or the plain title on its first line\n        — so `agents/coding/developer.book` signs as its Book title and not as its normalized identifier.\n    -   A run started without `--agent` reports exactly what it reported before.\n\n-   Fixed `MockedChat` typing animations blinking for messages without ids by assigning stable playback-only ids before rendering each simulated transcript.\n\n-   Fixed the rich `ptbk coder run` dashboard so an animated agent avatar can no longer overwrite its own UI in an\n    exact-width terminal pane:\n\n    -   The shared frame layout now leaves one physical terminal column unused, preventing boxed rows from\n        auto-wrapping and keeping incremental cursor-based redraws aligned with their logical frame rows.\n    -   Added a focused VS Code terminal preset and regression coverage for the terminal-width invariant.\n\n-   Added agent-specific prompt routing to `ptbk coder`:\n\n    -   A ready `[ ]` prompt can now target the Book passed in `--agent` with a backtick-delimited path, filename,\n        filename without `.book`, or the Book title from its first line. For example, a run using\n        `--agent agents/coding/developer.book` accepts `agents/coding/developer.book`, `developer.book`,\n        `developer`, and `Promptbook Developer` routing tokens.\n    -   Agent references work alongside the existing model and harness routing tokens, and `ptbk coder list --agent\n        <path.book>` previews the same agent-specific queue without starting a harness.\n    -   Added an Unslopper agent preset next to the developer preset in the local VS Code terminal scripts and\n        documented agent-specific routing on the `ptbk coder` landing page.\n\n-   The help of `ptbk` does not advertise the deprecated commands anymore. `run`, `login`, `make`, `prettify`, `test`,\n    `list-models`, `list-scrapers`, `start-agents-server` and `start-pipelines-server` are all leftovers of the old\n    pipeline system, yet nine of the fifteen commands which `ptbk --help` listed were exactly those, each one with its\n    own `Deprecated:` paragraph, so the listing which is supposed to introduce the CLI was mostly made of commands\n    nobody should start using. `ptbk --help`, and the same listing which plain `ptbk` prints when it asks for a\n    subcommand, now offers only the commands which are meant to be used - `coder`, `agent`, `agent-folder`,\n    `agents-server`, `about` and `hello`. Nothing was removed: every deprecated command still runs, still warns that it\n    is deprecated when it is used, still explains the deprecation in its own help - `ptbk run --help` - and is still\n    reachable through `ptbk help run`. Only the \"did you mean\" hint for a mistyped command stops pointing at them.\n    Being left out of the help is now simply a part of what deprecating a command means, written once in\n    `$deprecateCliCommand`, so any command deprecated later disappears from the help on its own.\n\n-   `ptbk` without a subcommand no longer falls back to the deprecated `ptbk run`. Until now `run` was registered as\n    the default command of the CLI, so everything which did not name a command - `ptbk ./write-cv.book`, a mistyped\n    `ptbk codr` or a stray option - was quietly handed over to the pipeline runner of the old system, which was the\n    last thing a deprecated command should be doing. Plain `ptbk` now asks to specify a subcommand and prints the\n    top-level help, exactly like `ptbk coder`, `ptbk agent`, `ptbk agent-folder` and `ptbk agents-server` already did\n    when they were called without one of their own subcommands, and that one shared behavior is now written once\n    instead of five times. Anything which is not a command is refused with `unknown command` and a \"did you mean\"\n    hint instead of being executed as a pipeline, so a script which still passes a book path to `ptbk` fails loudly\n    rather than appearing to succeed. `ptbk run` itself is untouched and keeps working for everyone who asks for it\n    explicitly. The command list in the help now starts with `coder`, followed by `agent`, `agent-folder` and\n    `agents-server`, and the deprecated commands of the old pipeline system are listed after them.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now saves the run trace of every prompt round, so a finished run can still be analyzed afterwards.\n    Until now the only durable record of a round was the one status line written into the prompt file: the live\n    runtime log holding everything the harness and the verification command had written was a temporary artifact,","numLines":60,"startLine":1,"totalLines":4936}}}

Two runs of the same harness, model and","originalFile":"-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and\n    thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now\n    names the agent which implemented it:\n\n    -   A prompt status line signs its work with the agent in front of the harness, as\n        `` [x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.13 23 minutes ``.\n        The `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status lines and the run trace of the round all report it, and a prompt continued\n        through `--git-changes continue` keeps the agent in each of its chronological `interrupted, continued by …`\n        reports.\n    -   The reported name is the display name of the Book — its `META FULLNAME`, or the plain title on its first line\n        — so `agents/coding/developer.book` signs as its Book title and not as its normalized identifier.\n    -   A run started without `--agent` reports exactly what it reported before.\n\n-   Fixed `MockedChat` typing animations blinking for messages without ids by assigning stable playback-only ids before rendering each simulated transcript.\n\n-   Fixed the rich `ptbk coder run` dashboard so an animated agent avatar can no longer overwrite its own UI in an\n    exact-width terminal pane:\n\n    -   The shared frame layout now leaves one physical terminal column unused, preventing boxed rows from\n        auto-wrapping and keeping incremental cursor-based redraws aligned with their logical frame rows.\n    -   Added a focused VS Code terminal preset and regression coverage for the terminal-width invariant.\n\n-   Added agent-specific prompt routing to `ptbk coder`:\n\n    -   A ready `[ ]` prompt can now target the Book passed in `--agent` with a backtick-delimited path, filename,\n        filename without `.book`, or the Book title from its first line. For example, a run using\n        `--agent agents/coding/developer.book` accepts `agents/coding/developer.book`, `developer.book`,\n        `developer`, and `Promptbook Developer` routing tokens.\n    -   Agent references work alongside the existing model and harness routing tokens, and `ptbk coder list --agent\n        <path.book>` previews the same agent-specific queue without starting a harness.\n    -   Added an Unslopper agent preset next to the developer preset in the local VS Code terminal scripts and\n        documented agent-specific routing on the `ptbk coder` landing page.\n\n-   The help of `ptbk` does not advertise the deprecated commands anymore. `run`, `login`, `make`, `prettify`, `test`,\n    `list-models`, `list-scrapers`, `start-agents-server` and `start-pipelines-server` are all leftovers of the old\n    pipeline system, yet nine of the fifteen commands which `ptbk --help` listed were exactly those, each one with its\n    own `Deprecated:` paragraph, so the listing which is supposed to introduce the CLI was mostly made of commands\n    nobody should start using. `ptbk --help`, and the same listing which plain `ptbk` prints when it asks for a\n    subcommand, now offers only the commands which are meant to be used - `coder`, `agent`, `agent-folder`,\n    `agents-server`, `about` and `hello`. Nothing was removed: every deprecated command still runs, still warns that it\n    is deprecated when it is used, still explains the deprecation in its own help - `ptbk run --help` - and is still\n    reachable through `ptbk help run`. Only the \"did you mean\" hint for a mistyped command stops pointing at them.\n    Being left out of the help is now simply a part of what deprecating a command means, written once in\n    `$deprecateCliCommand`, so any command deprecated later disappears from the help on its own.\n\n-   `ptbk` without a subcommand no longer falls back to the deprecated `ptbk run`. Until now `run` was registered as\n    the default command of the CLI, so everything which did not name a command - `ptbk ./write-cv.book`, a mistyped\n    `ptbk codr` or a stray option - was quietly handed over to the pipeline runner of the old system, which was the\n    last thing a deprecated command should be doing. Plain `ptbk` now asks to specify a subcommand and prints the\n    top-level help, exactly like `ptbk coder`, `ptbk agent`, `ptbk agent-folder` and `ptbk agents-server` already did\n    when they were called without one of their own subcommands, and that one shared behavior is now written once\n    instead of five times. Anything which is not a command is refused with `unknown command` and a \"did you mean\"\n    hint instead of being executed as a pipeline, so a script which still passes a book path to `ptbk` fails loudly\n    rather than appearing to succeed. `ptbk run` itself is untouched and keeps working for everyone who asks for it\n    explicitly. The command list in the help now starts with `coder`, followed by `agent`, `agent-folder` and\n    `agents-server`, and the deprecated commands of the old pipeline system are listed after them.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now saves the run trace of every prompt round, so a finished run can still be analyzed afterwards.\n    Until now the only durable record of a round was the one status line written into the prompt file: the live\n    runtime log holding everything the harness and the verification command had written was a temporary artifact,\n    deleted as soon as a successful round was over unless `--preserve-logs` was passed, and lost together with the\n    reasoning, the tool calls and the diffs of the run. Each round now writes `prompts/traces/<prompt-file-name>.md`\n    - a trace named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to, with the same `-2` section suffix the temporary\n    scripts of a multi-section prompt file already use. The trace pairs the metadata of the round - which prompt and\n    section it implemented, whether it succeeded or failed, the harness, model, thinking level and login method which\n    ran it, how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran, the verification\n    command, the start, end and duration, and the error which ended a failed round - with the untouched runtime log\n    of the harness. Because the trace is written before the round is committed, it lands in the very same commit as\n    the prompt it describes, and a task whose isolated worktree cannot be merged back carries its trace into the\n    failure commit instead. A failed round is traced too, next to the `.error.log` it already wrote. Re-running the\n    same prompt overwrites its trace and leaves the earlier ones in the git history.\n\n-   `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server` no longer walk into a full disk. A coding round writes prompt and log\n    artifacts, lets the harness rewrite the project, may install npm packages, may create a git worktree for\n    `--isolate` and usually runs a build, so a run started without enough space used to die somewhere in the middle,\n    after the coding agent had already rewritten a part of the project. The free disk space is now measured before\n    anything is installed or written: with less than 2 GB left the command refuses to start and says how much space\n    is left, how much is needed and how to get it back, instead of failing later with a raw filesystem error. The\n    same measurement is repeated while the run is in progress - at the checkpoints where `ptbk coder` can stop\n    anyway, so it is checked before every round, every verification and every commit - and once less than 1 GB is\n    left the run reports the same warning and pauses there, waiting for the disk space to be freed and for `P` to\n    resume it. The limit to keep running is lower than the limit to start, because interrupting a round which is\n    already in progress costs more than not starting one. A run started with `--no-questions` never pauses, because\n    there is nobody who could free the disk space and resume it - it reports the warning and keeps going. A platform\n    which cannot report its free disk space never stops a run.\n\n-   Added `--no-questions` to every `ptbk coder` command which can stop and wait for an answer it does not strictly\n    need. `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server` still do all their work, but no longer ask anything: installing\n    a missing coding harness, updating an outdated one, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing\n    harness ignore rules to `.gitignore` are all skipped and reported together with the command which does them\n    manually, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it. Because an outdated\n    harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, `--no-questions` also skips the npm latest-version\n    lookup which would only lead to a question, which is what the never released `--no-harness-update` used to do -\n    that flag is replaced by `--no-questions` and is gone. The one combination which can not work,\n    `--no-auto --no-questions`, is refused right away instead of waiting forever for a confirmation nobody may be\n    asked for. `ptbk coder verify` does not take the flag, because walking through finished prompts and asking about\n    each of them is the only thing it does.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` no longer answers a harness which is not logged in with a wall of raw CLI output. A harness whose\n    login is missing or whose session has expired now fails with a short branded `AuthenticationError` which names\n    the harness, quotes the one sentence the harness itself reported - such as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session\n    expired and could not be refreshed` - and says exactly how to sign in again, for example by running `claude` and\n    then the `/login` command inside it. How each harness is signed in is described once, next to how it is installed\n    and detected, and the failure is recognized once for every harness and for every command\n    which runs prompts, so `coder run`, `coder server` and `coder ping` all report it the same way. The terminal and\n    the `.error.log` file written next to the prompt both show those instructions on their own now, instead of\n    following them with a stack trace of a failure nobody can debug. Because no retry of a harness which is not\n    logged in can ever succeed, such a prompt is also no longer retried three times with the `--wait-after-error`\n    delay in between - the instructions are shown right away.\n\n-   Fixed the wall of `npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings printed when installing `ptbk`:\n\n    -   The Vercel AI SDK providers `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google` and `@ai-sdk/deepseek` were still on the\n        generation which accepts only Zod 3, while the rest of the ecosystem - the Agents Server, `@openai/agents`,\n        `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` - needs Zod 4. No single Zod could satisfy both sides, so npm reported a conflict\n        for every one of those packages. They are upgraded to the newest generation which accepts both Zod 3 and\n        Zod 4 and still runs on Node.js 18, so the supported Node.js versions of Promptbook do not change, and\n        `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` is migrated to the model interface of that generation. Settings\n        given as `additionalChatSettings` are now passed to the model call instead of to the model constructor,\n        which is where the Vercel AI SDK expects them, and the `userId` option is no longer sent as the `user`\n        setting, because it has become specific to each provider.\n    -   Generated packages no longer publish dependencies which only look like imports. Package generation infers\n        dependencies by reading the generated bundle, and it used to count module specifiers written inside the\n        source-code templates of the transpilers, so `@promptbook/core` published `zod`, `dotenv` and\n        `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as runtime dependencies although it never imports any of them. The pinned `zod` in\n        particular forced one exact Zod version onto every project which installs Promptbook.\n    -   Generated packages no longer carry the `overrides` field of the repository. npm honors overrides only in the\n        root project of an installation, so publishing them only left a dangling reference to a dependency which the\n        published package does not declare.\n\n    What remains after this are three warnings about React 19 coming from packages inside `swagger-ui-react`, which\n    are declared by projects outside of Promptbook.\n\n-   The hero headline of the **ptbk coder** landing page now rotates through seven claims instead of saying one\n    thing forever. Every claim is written once in a single configuration the rotating headline, the page tagline\n    and the sharing image all read, and the claims crossfade with a slight vertical slide - the claim which leaves\n    rises out of the headline while the next one rises into it. All claims share one grid cell, so the headline\n    keeps the height of the tallest of them and nothing around it moves while they rotate. The same reserved\n    height finally balances the hero: together with a terminal text size tuned one step down, the copy column now\n    reaches almost as high as the live terminal next to it, instead of floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defines. Visitors whose system prefers reduced motion keep the first claim without rotation.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` overwriting configuration the project already owns. Existing `package.json` scripts and\n    `.vscode/settings.json` settings are now kept verbatim and only genuinely missing ones are added. Files a default\n    script points at, like `agents/developer.book`, `AGENTS.md` and `prompts/templates/common.md`, are created only\n    together with the script which references them, so a project with its own `coder:run` no longer receives an unused\n    default agent. `ptbk coder init` also initializes the `test-for-ptbk-coder` npm script which the default\n    `coder:run` uses as its verification command.\n\n-   Rebalanced the hero of the **ptbk coder** landing page, whose live terminal used to be much taller than the copy\n    next to it and left the headline, the install command and the buttons floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defined:\n\n    -   The terminal window is now never wider than the character grid it draws, so a layout with more width than the\n        widest supported terminal - a tablet, a phone in landscape - gets a centered window instead of a window with an\n        empty half, and it fills the height of the copy column whenever the copy is the taller one.\n    -   A terminal row is now as tight as a real terminal emulator draws it, which both shortens the sample session by\n        about one tenth and keeps the frames of the dashboard boxes connected.\n    -   The box drawing characters, the shade of the progress bar and the status marks are missing from the latin\n        subset of the terminal font, so they were drawn from the fallback which `next/font` derives from a\n        **proportional** font - about one and a half character cells wide and shorter than one row, which broke every\n        box border of the dashboard into detached segments. The terminal font now falls back to the monospace fonts of\n        the system, so those characters are drawn one cell wide and one row tall and the boxes are drawn as continuous\n        frames.\n    -   The hero copy is now read at hero size: the headline and the subheadline grow with the viewport, but only as\n        far as their own column can carry them, so the headline keeps its two lines from the narrowest phone to the\n        widest desktop.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` so it no longer creates an `AGENT_CODING.md` quick-reference file.\n-   Redesigned the three core benefit illustrations on the **ptbk coder** landing page with detailed terminal,\n    portable-agent, and synchronized-commit scenes, plus proportional graphics and a more readable tablet layout.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` to preserve a non-empty `prompts/` directory instead of adding placeholder boilerplate\n    prompts while it initializes the remaining coder files.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder list`, a read-only queue preview that lists ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority\n    groups without starting a harness. Its optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and\n    `--max-priority` filters let you preview exactly the queue a selected runner would receive.\n\n-   Added a live GitHub star counter and **Star on GitHub** call to action to the **ptbk coder** landing page.\n\n-   Added support for plain markdown prompts without a status checkbox in **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder run` and\n    `ptbk coder server` now treat them as ready prompts at priority `0`, then insert the normal live `[^]` status line\n    before their content as processing begins and finish them through the usual `[x]` or `[!]` flow.\n\n-   Added queue opt-out markers to **ptbk coder**. `[.]` now behaves like `[-]`, keeping that prompt out of the queue,\n    and `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown prompt file excludes the entire file from `run`, `list`, and\n    `server`.\n\n-   Added project-local harness ignore rules to **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder init` now adds the rules for every supported\n    harness, including `.qwen`; `ptbk coder run`, `ptbk coder server`, and `ptbk coder ping` detect a missing selected\n    harness rule and use the same interactive `[y/N]` confirmation as harness installation updates before adding it.\n\n-   Fixed globally installing `ptbk` on Node.js 26, including macOS arm64. `ptbk coder` can now be installed without\n    `better-sqlite3` 11 falling back to a native build against removed V8 APIs; the generated CLI now receives\n    `better-sqlite3` 12.11.1, which supplies the matching Node 26 binary.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server production build failing when its Edge middleware reached standalone SQLite code.\n    SQLite registry loading now lives in a Node.js-only module, and custom-domain routing reads its needed federation\n    settings through the middleware's supplied Supabase client. Edge middleware can therefore route configured domains\n    without compiling `better-sqlite3` into its bundle.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder --harness openai-codex --model default` failing for everyone signed in to OpenAI Codex with a\n    ChatGPT account. `default` silently stood for `gpt-5.2-codex`, which such an account rejects with\n    _\"The 'gpt-5.2-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account\"_ — so both\n    `ptbk coder ping` and `ptbk coder run` died before doing any work.\n\n    -   `--model default` now overrides **no model at all** for OpenAI Codex: Codex is started without `--model` and\n        keeps the model from its own configuration _(`~/.codex/config.toml`)_, exactly like `--model default` already\n        worked for GitHub Copilot. Whatever a ChatGPT-account login is allowed to use therefore works.\n    -   Naming a model explicitly, for example `--model gpt-5.2-codex`, is unchanged, and `--model` is still required\n        for OpenAI Codex.\n    -   For `gemini` and `qwen-code`, `default` keeps standing for their concrete default model, because those CLIs\n        have no configured default to fall back to.\n    -   When Codex picks the model itself, the reported price is estimated from the fallback pricing, because only\n        Codex knows which model it really used.\n\n-   Fixed **ptbk coder** updating a coding harness with `npm install -g` even when npm does not own that harness. A\n    Codex installed by the official standalone installer was reported as outdated and \"updated\" into a _second_ Codex\n    inside the active Node prefix, while the Codex which actually runs stayed on its old version — and which of the two\n    was used from then on depended on the active Node version.\n\n    -   Before offering an update, `ptbk coder` now resolves which file the harness command really executes _(following\n        symbolic links, using the very same `PATH` which runs the harness)_ and recognizes whether it belongs to a\n        global npm installation, a standalone installation, or Homebrew.\n    -   A **standalone installation is updated with its own updater** — `codex update` for OpenAI Codex — and a\n        **Homebrew installation is never touched**, only `brew upgrade …` is printed. When the harness command cannot\n        be traced to any of these, `ptbk coder` says so and leaves it alone instead of guessing, because\n        `npm install -g` would install a second copy next to it.\n    -   The outdated-harness warning now also prints the resolved command path and how it was installed, and the\n        confirmation question names the exact command which is about to run, so an update can no longer be approved\n        without knowing what it does.\n    -   Installing a harness which is missing altogether is unchanged: it is still installed globally through npm.\n\n-   Added the singular `WRITING RULE` keyword as an equivalent variant of `WRITING RULES`, exactly like `RULE` and\n    `RULES` are interchangeable. Both spellings are parsed, applied, documented, and syntax-highlighted identically, so\n    a single writing constraint no longer has to be written in plural.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server starting one more pm2 process of the same agent project on every single start, which\n    eventually took the whole server down.\n\n    -   Every project runtime is registered under a stable pm2 process name, and a project was expected to be replaced\n        rather than duplicated because it is deleted right before it is started again. That delete was **skipped\n        whenever pm2 could not be asked for its process list**, and `pm2 start` appends a second process instead of\n        refusing a name it already knows, so each start added one more copy of the same project.\n    -   The process list could not be read because `pm2 jlist` embeds a full environment snapshot into every listed\n        process — roughly 70 kB each — while its output was capped at one megabyte. A dozen projects were enough to\n        exceed that cap, after which **every** pm2 query failed with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` and reported\n        every process as unknown. Each new duplicate made the output larger, so the failure never recovered on its own.\n    -   Every duplicate got its own port but the project's dev command kept binding the port it had chosen itself, so\n        all but one copy crash-looped on `EADDRINUSE`, and pm2 restarted them hundreds of times per hour until the VPS\n        ran out of threads (`pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable`) and the Agents Server itself was\n        killed.\n    -   Deleting a project process no longer depends on reading the process list: it is always attempted, only pm2\n        itself reporting an unknown name counts as \"already gone\", and any other failure is reported instead of\n        swallowed — so a project is now left alone rather than duplicated when pm2 misbehaves. Because `pm2 delete`\n        removes every process sharing one name, a server which already accumulated duplicates converges back to a\n        single process per project.\n\n-   Added the **Qwen Code** harness, so `ptbk coder` now drives seven coding agents instead of six.\n\n    -   `ptbk coder run --harness qwen-code --model qwen3.8-max` runs the whole prompt queue through the Qwen Code CLI,\n        and every other harness-aware command — `ptbk coder ping`, `ptbk coder server`, `ptbk agent exec`, `CliAgent`\n        and the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable — accepts `qwen-code` the same way.\n    -   Like `openai-codex` and `gemini`, Qwen Code **requires an explicit `--model`**; `--model default` resolves to\n        `qwen3.8-max`. Its global `@qwen-code/qwen-code` installation is checked and updated before the first prompt,\n        just like the other harnesses. Qwen Code exposes no reasoning-effort flag, so `--thinking-level` does not\n        apply to it.\n    -   Price estimation of harnesses which do not report their own token counts is now shared between Qwen Code and\n        Gemini instead of being written twice.\n\n-   Fixed generated `ptbk` prompt emoji tags so `coder add`, `coder generate-boilerplates`, refactor prompt generation, and `coder find-fresh-emoji-tags` share one Unicode-valid single-pictogram catalogue instead of a duplicated legacy list containing non-emoji symbols. The emoji-tag scan cache now records the candidate catalogue fingerprint and rescans when it changes, so an already assigned tag such as `[✨🛼]` is not mistaken for a fresh tag after an update.\n\n-   Added remaining subscription-limit visibility to the rich **ptbk coder** terminal dashboard.\n\n    -   The `Session` box now lists every rolling limit a selected harness reports, including its remaining percentage\n        and reset time. It does not assume a fixed pair of windows, so a 5-hour, weekly, model-specific, or future\n        additional limit all render as separate aligned rows.\n    -   OpenAI Codex reads its current account snapshot through the Codex app-server protocol, while Claude Code\n        reuses its normal `stream-json` rate-limit events instead of spending a separate quota-only prompt. Other\n        harnesses keep their existing behavior until they implement the same optional runner capability.\n    -   Updated the **ptbk coder** landing-page terminal demo and pacing copy to show the new 5-hour and 7-day\n        subscription rows.\n\n-   Let you decide what **ptbk coder** does with a dirty working tree. The clean-working-tree guard used to be a yes/no\n    question — either the coder refused to start, or `--ignore-git-changes` waved the changes through. The far more\n    common case had no answer at all: a run that was killed or crashed mid-task, leaving half-finished work in the tree\n    and one prompt stuck in the in-progress `[^]` status. The only way forward was to throw that work away.\n\n    -   **The new `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` replaces `--ignore-git-changes`**, which is gone; use\n        `--git-changes ignore` instead. `fail` stays the default and now says in its error which of the other two modes\n        to reach for.\n    -   **`--git-changes continue` resumes the interrupted prompt** with its uncommitted changes still in place. It\n        expects **exactly one** prompt in the `[^]` status and refuses to guess otherwise: finding none or finding\n        several fails with a message naming the prompts it found, because the changes in the tree cannot be attributed\n        to a single task. Only that one round runs on the dirty tree — once it is committed, every later round expects a\n        clean working tree again. It cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree is checked out from the\n        last commit and would leave exactly those changes behind, or `--test-before yes-and-fix`, which has no\n        unmodified project state to verify and repair.\n    -   **A prompt one harness started and another one finished says so in chronological order.** A resumed status\n        now reads `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high` - Implementation in progress ``,\n        and the `[x]` and `[!]` lines keep that report.
