The current and latest commit cards, plus every pending-commit row, now visibly show the commit subject, full hash, and authored date.\n    -   Factored the time-behind suffix out of `buildDeploymentDriftLabel` into a new shared `buildDeploymentTimeBehindLabel` helper so the same localized `N days behind` text powers both the current-deployment card and the pending-commits card without duplication.\n    -   Added a new `GET /api/admin/update/log` route that streams the full persisted `self-update.log` file (gated by `isUserGlobalAdmin`) together with a `Content-Disposition` filename, backed by a new `readVpsSelfUpdateLogFileContent` helper in `vpsSelfUpdate.ts`.\n    -   When the latest update job's status is `failed`, the Update job card now shows **Copy log** and **Download log** buttons that hit the new endpoint and reuse the shared `downloadBlob` / `parseFilenameFromContentDisposition` helpers (same flow as the existing Backup export), so the admin can quickly share the full installer log with the developers for debugging instead of only seeing the truncated terminal tail.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server `/admin/update` self-update failing on the standalone VPS during the post-compile `Linting and checking validity of types ...` phase with `next-build exited with code null.` (the Node build process was being killed by the OS, typically by the OOM killer, after webpack had already retried minification multiple times). The shared `other/vps/install.sh` `build_agents_server` step now sets `PTBK_AGENTS_SERVER_IGNORE_NEXT_VALIDATION=true` so the VPS production build skips the duplicate Next.js lint + TypeScript validation step that is already enforced by repository CI, matching the existing CLI materialized-runtime build path and letting the self-update finish reliably on memory-constrained VPS hosts.\n\n-   Changed the Agents Server durable chat progress card so each preparation phase shows the **real runtime state** that has actually been resolved so far, instead of a fixed scripted blurb that was identical for every chat turn:\n\n    -   `createUserChatProgressCard` now accepts a `UserChatProgressContext` object and composes the `now`/`next` markdown from real signals — resolved agent name, attachment count, configured tool count and friendly tool labels (e.g. `web browser`, `web search`, `email sending`), knowledge-source count, calendar/email/project integrations, the resolved LLM provider title, and whether the AgentKit runtime came from the in-process cache.\n    -   `createRunUserChatJobExecutionContext` builds that context incrementally as the worker resolves new information and forwards it through `reportProgress` at every phase, so the user sees, for example, **\"Loading the instructions and configured commitments for agent Cooking Coach (2 knowledge sources)\"** instead of the previous static **\"Preparing the agent instructions and context needed for this request.\"**\n    -   The `starting_response` update is now emitted **after** the AgentKit cache lookup completes, so the progress text can name the actual provider (e.g. **\"Calling the language model via OpenAI\"**) and call out whether the agent had to be prepared fresh.\n    -   Added a small `resolveUserChatProgressToolHighlights` helper that maps technical commitment tool identifiers (`web_search`, `useBrowser`, `send_email`, …) to short user-facing labels and excludes the internal `agent_progress` / `assistant_preparation` tools that should never appear as user-relevant capabilities.\n    -   Updated the queued-message lifecycle copy to reflect the actual queueing state (**\"Your message is waiting in the queue for the next available worker to pick it up.\"**) and updated `userChatMessageLifecycle.test.ts` accordingly.\n\n-   Added a new `Octopus 3D 4` built-in avatar visual as a smoother, blobbier continuation of `Octopus 3D 3`, and promoted it to the new shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`:\n\n    -   Reused the seeded `Octopus3` morphology profile together with the shared projected-eye and projected-mouth helpers so the new proper-3D octopus stays consistent with the rest of the octopus family without duplicating face-rendering logic.\n    -   Rendered the whole octopus as one continuous blobby mesh sampled at a higher latitude/longitude resolution so the silhouette reads as a round, real-octopus body with eight tentacle lobes that smoothly fuse into the mantle instead of attaching as separate ribbons.\n    -   Drove the tentacle motion with a combined primary, secondary, and slow-curl sine harmonic per lobe so the tentacles wave naturally and continuously, like a real octopus drifting in water, while remaining cute and simple.\n    -   Added a richer multi-pass shading pipeline (key light, rim light, soft gloss highlight, seeded pigment spots, and per-patch outline) on top of the existing palette tones, so the silhouette feels textured and visually appealing without leaving the simple flat-stylized look.\n    -   Kept avatar pointer tracking on both the full mesh silhouette and the projected eyes — the head turns toward the mouse cursor more responsively than `Octopus 3D 3` and the eyes track the pointer inside the rotated head.\n    -   Switched the shared `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL_ID` to `octopus3d4`, updated the Agents Server `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL` metadata default + allowed-values note to include `OCTOPUS3D4`, and added a backwards-compatible database migration that upgrades existing `OCTOPUS3D3` defaults to `OCTOPUS3D4` while preserving any administrator-customized value.\n\n-   Fixed broken access control on chat history, chat feedback, and agent CRUD routes of Agents Server. Multiple route handlers guarded themselves with `getCurrentUser()` (i.e. \"the caller is logged in\") but never checked that the **specific record** being read, modified, or deleted belonged to the caller or that the caller was an administrator, so any authenticated user — including self-registered unprivileged users — could read, mutate, or destroy data that belonged to other users / other agents:\n\n    -   `/api/chat-history` (`GET`/`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/[id]` (`DELETE`), `/api/chat-history/export` (`GET`), `/api/chat-feedback` (`GET`/`DELETE`), and `/api/chat-feedback/export` (`GET`) returned (or deleted) the **entire** `ChatHistory` / `ChatFeedback` tables across every agent and user. These endpoints power the admin-only `/admin/chat-history` and `/admin/chat-feedback` screens — which expose IPs, anonymous `userNote`s, and `expectedAnswer`s across all agents — so they are now gated by `isUserAdmin()` instead of `getCurrentUser()`, returning `401 Unauthorized` for non-administrators. The two admin pages and the agent-context-menu entries that link to them were updated to require admin as well, so non-administrators no longer see dead-end links to those screens.\n    -   `PATCH /api/agents/[agentName]` (rename / change visibility) and `DELETE /api/agents/[agentName]` (tombstone) never resolved the agent's owner. Both handlers now resolve the target agent through a new shared `findAgentForCallerWriteAccess` helper that combines `findOwnedAgentByIdentifier` (reusing the same ownership primitive as the v1 management API) with an `isUserAdmin()` admin override, and reject with `404 Not Found` when the agent does not belong to the caller and the caller is not an administrator. The visibility update is now scoped to the resolved row by primary key instead of matching every agent that shares the supplied name or permanent id. The new helper also covers legacy `ADMIN_PASSWORD` administrators that have no database user id.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in three additional Agents Server endpoints that accepted a caller-supplied URL and fetched it server-side without authentication and without the existing `assertSafeUrl` SSRF guard:\n\n    -   `/api/page-preview/screenshot` opened the URL in a headless Playwright browser (which executes JavaScript on the fetched page) and returned a PNG screenshot. The only validation was that the scheme was `http:` or `https:`, so an unauthenticated attacker could screenshot `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (AWS / GCP / Azure metadata service), or any RFC-1918 private address.\n    -   `/api/page-preview/check` performed a server-side `fetch` (HEAD with `redirect: follow`) through `checkIfUrlCanBeEmbedded` with the same lack of validation.\n    -   `/api/team-agent-profile` called `fetchAgentProfile` against any URL that passed the structural `isValidAgentUrl` check and forwarded the internal team access token to the target. The same-origin check inside `createTeamInternalAgentAccessHeaders` already prevented the token from leaking to truly cross-origin URLs, but the SSRF itself was unblocked.\n\n    All three endpoints now require authentication (`getCurrentUser` returns `401 Unauthorized` for anonymous requests) and validate the destination URL through `assertSafeUrl` (the same helper that already protects `/api/scrape`) before any outbound `fetch` / `page.goto`, returning `400 Bad Request` for non-HTTP(S) schemes and private/internal IP destinations (loopback, RFC 1918, link-local / cloud-metadata, shared address space, IPv6 ULA / link-local / loopback). The chat citation iframe-fallback feature is unaffected because it runs inside the authenticated chat UI and previews public citation URLs. The `[👣][🧠]` TODO in `isValidAgentUrl` is resolved by keeping that function a pure structural validator and documenting that callers reaching untrusted networks must apply `assertSafeUrl` themselves.\n\n-   Fixed unauthenticated abuse of server-side paid AI APIs in Agents Server. Five route handlers proxied directly to paid third-party providers (OpenAI, ElevenLabs) using the **server's API keys** without any authentication check, so any anonymous client could drain the configured API credit and exhaust quotas by repeatedly calling them. All five routes are now protected by a new shared `guardPaidApiRequest` utility that combines authentication and per-identity sliding-window rate limiting (DRY for all paid-proxy endpoints):\n\n    -   `/api/chat` and `/api/chat-streaming` were OpenAI smoke-test endpoints with no frontend usage. They are now gated behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` and return `404` in production so they cannot be exploited even if the deployment exposes them.\n    -   `/api/openai/v1/audio/transcriptions` now requires authentication (signed session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer ptbk_…` API key), enforces a 25 MB upload size limit, validates the `model` parameter against an allowlist of supported OpenAI transcription models (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `whisper-1`), validates `language` against ISO-639-1, and truncates the optional transcription `prompt` to 800 characters.\n    -   `/api/elevenlabs/tts` now requires authentication and validates the caller-supplied `voiceId` against the strict ElevenLabs format (15–40 alphanumeric characters), preventing path-segment injection into the upstream URL and rejecting unknown voices that would still bill the ElevenLabs account.\n    -   `/api/images/[filename]` now requires authentication and validates `modelName`, `size`, `quality`, and `style` query parameters against fixed allowlists (DALL·E / Gemini image models, supported sizes, `standard`/`hd`, `vivid`/`natural`) before forwarding to the paid image generation provider.\n    -   The shared guard applies a per-identity sliding-window rate limit on top of authentication — by username for cookie sessions, by hashed API key for bearer auth, and by request IP for any anonymous fallback. Budgets are tier-specific (60/min for transcription and TTS, 20/min for image generation), so a single compromised account cannot sustain large bills. Rejected requests receive `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header.\n\n-   Fixed authentication bypass in Agents Server `validateApiKey`: the helper previously treated the presence of any `sessionToken` cookie as proof of a valid browser session, so any client could forge `Cookie: sessionToken=anything` and gain unauthenticated access to every endpoint behind `validateApiKey` (including the OpenAI-compatible chat-completion routes that consume server-side API credits). The helper now parses the cookie value with the existing `parseSessionToken` HMAC-signature verifier and only accepts the request when the signature matches, restoring the original intent of the browser-session shortcut without trusting attacker-supplied cookies.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server directory and chat-sidebar reads for standalone VPS and Supabase deployments:\n\n    -   Added SQLite read indexes for active agent/folder directory scans, chat sidebar lists, and active chat job/timeout polling used by the homepage, agent navigation, and chat pages.\n    -   Added matching PostgreSQL indexes for active agent/folder directory reads and creation-time chat sidebar ordering.\n    -   Invalidated cached active organization snapshots after agent source, visibility, create, delete, and restore mutations so optimized homepage/menu data refreshes immediately.\n\n-   Fixed timing attack vulnerability in Agents Server admin password verification: all three comparison sites (`isUserGlobalAdmin`, `getCurrentUser`, `authenticateUser`) now use a shared `isAdminPasswordEqual` utility that calls Node.js's `timingSafeEqual` (from the `crypto` module) instead of JavaScript's `===` operator, preventing character-by-character password inference via response-time measurement.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server durable chat progress so new agent responses show structured real progress from the queued and preparation phases instead of a synthetic immediate pre-answer:\n\n    -   Queued assistant placeholders now render a progress card with current step, next step, and checklist state.\n    -   The durable chat worker updates that card while it reads context, prepares the agent, checks available tools/inputs, and starts the response.\n    -   The `agent_progress` tool instructions now ask the real agent to report concise user-facing decisions, actions, and results without exposing hidden chain-of-thought or raw technical details.\n\n-   Fixed SSRF vulnerability in the Agents Server `/api/scrape` endpoint:\n\n    -   The endpoint now requires authentication — unauthenticated requests receive a `401 Unauthorized` response.\n    -   Added URL validation via a new `assertSafeUrl` utility that rejects non-HTTP(S) schemes and destination hostnames that resolve to private/internal IP ranges (RFC 1918: `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`, `192.168.x`; loopback `127.x`; link-local / cloud-metadata `169.254.x`; shared address space `100.64.x`; IPv6 ULA, link-local, and loopback). Blocked requests receive a `400 Bad Request` response.\n\n-   Fixed package publishing for `@promptbook/cli` by marking the `ptbk coder server` HTTP/UI helpers as CLI-only instead of never-publishable, matching the existing CLI command import chain.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder find-unwritten` command that lists all prompt sections whose body still contains the `@@@` authoring placeholder:\n\n    -   Prints a summary line (done / for agent / to be written counts) followed by a numbered list of unwritten prompts with their file path, line number, and first summary line.\n    -   Accepts `--priority <n>` to apply the same minimum-priority filter used by `ptbk coder run`.\n    -   Reuses the existing `listPromptsToBeWritten` / `printPromptsToBeWritten` utilities so the detection logic stays in one place.\n\n-   Added `--agent <agent-book-path>` option to `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server`:\n\n    -   Accepts a path to a `.book` file (relative to the current working directory) whose compiled system message is prepended to each coding prompt before the task text.\n    -   Can be combined with `--context`: the agent system message is inserted first, followed by the task prompt, and finally the context — so the harness sees agent instructions → task → additional context.\n    -   Example: `ptbk coder run --harness github-copilot --model gpt-5.4 --thinking-level xhigh --context AGENTS.md --agent agents/coding-expert.book`\n\n-   `ptbk coder init` now automatically generates 5 prompt boilerplate files after setting up the project configuration.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder server` command that runs the same prompt-processing logic as `ptbk coder run` but keeps the process alive and serves a kanban web UI on a configurable port (default `4441`):\n\n    -   The server polls for new prompt files every 5 seconds instead of exiting when all prompts are done or none are ready, making it suitable as a long-running background service.\n    -   A kanban board at `http://localhost:4441` shows all prompt sections grouped into four columns: **To Do**, **Not Ready**, **Done**, and **Failed**.\n    -   Each card is clickable and opens a Trello-style edit modal where the prompt text can be modified and saved back to the source file immediately.\n    -   A **Play / Pause** button in the browser header is kept in sync with the CLI pause state; clicking it calls the same `requestPause` / `requestResume` functions used by the `p` key in the terminal.\n    -   The HTTP server exposes a small REST API: `GET /api/prompts`, `GET /api/status`, `POST /api/pause`, `POST /api/resume`, and `PUT /api/prompts/update`.\n    -   All options from `ptbk coder run` are supported (`--harness`, `--model`, `--thinking-level`, `--context`, `--test`, `--wait`, `--priority`, `--no-commit`, etc.) plus a new `--port` option (or `PTBK_CODER_SERVER_PORT` env var).\n    -   The frontend source lives in `apps/coder-server/index.html` and is served inline by the Node.js HTTP server (no build step required).\n\n-   Added a VSCode extension (`apps/vscode-extension`) for the Book language that provides syntax highlighting for `.book` and `.ptbk` files. The TextMate grammar (`syntaxes/book.tmLanguage.json`) is dynamically generated from `COMMITMENT_REGISTRY` by running `npm run generate-vscode-grammar`, ensuring the extension always reflects the current set of commitment keywords. Publishing to the Visual Studio Code Marketplace is available through `npm run build:vscode-extension -- --publish`, which generates the grammar, syncs a Marketplace-safe extension version from the root `package.json`, publishes with `vsce`, and creates the VSIX artifact.\n\n-   Fixed `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting incorrectly highlighting the local part of email addresses (e.g. `team@foo.bar`) as agent references. `@`-style references now require whitespace or start-of-line before the `@` sign, so only `@Paul` (with preceding whitespace) is highlighted, not `team@foo.bar`. Removed a now-redundant manual preceding-character check that duplicated this logic.\n\n-   Improved `<BookEditor/>` syntax highlighting to dynamically detect commitments — any line starting with one or more all-uppercase words (minimum 2 characters each) is now highlighted as a commitment keyword, without relying on a hardcoded list of known commitment types. Lines starting with a dash or a single uppercase letter are not affected. Special commitment types (`NOTE`, `NOTES`, `NONCE`, `TODO`) retain their distinct colors, and `FROM`/`IMPORT`/`IMPORTS`/`TEAM` retain agent-reference link highlighting.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server VPS installation failing on the first run with a Node.js out-of-memory crash during the Next.js production build. The `ptbk agents-server build` command now passes `--max-old-space-size=4096` in `NODE_OPTIONS` when spawning the webpack compilation process, allowing the ~1.9 GiB peak heap usage to succeed within the swap-backed memory budget enforced by the installer. Existing `NODE_OPTIONS` values are preserved; the flag is only injected when no `--max-old-space-size` is already set.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server file upload URLs for self-contained S3 to hide the internal bucket name, path prefix, and directory structure. Files are now stored under a content-addressed key (`{hash[0]}/{hash[1]}/{sha256}/{filename}`) and served through a new Next.js proxy route (`/s3/{hex}/{hex}/{hash}/{filename}`) so the public URL is unguessable and reveals no internal storage details. Old-style URLs (e.g. `/s3/promptbook-files/ptbk-agents/user/files/…`) remain accessible for backwards compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed citation source previews in Agents Server chat failing silently when the target page blocks iframe embedding via `X-Frame-Options` (e.g. `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`). The chat modal now checks embeddability server-side before rendering and falls back to a server-taken screenshot with an \"Open in new tab\" link when the page cannot be framed.\n\n-   Optimized Agents Server database layer to prevent the server from becoming unresponsive under load:\n\n    -   Added `connectionTimeoutMillis` (15 s) to the shared PostgreSQL connection pool so queries fail fast when all connections are busy instead of queuing indefinitely — the root cause of the server becoming completely unresponsive after a period of high traffic.\n    -   Increased the default pool size from 10 to 20 connections (configurable via `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` environment variable) to handle more concurrent chat-stream polling and atomic-SQL operations without exhausting the pool.\n    -   Added `idleTimeoutMillis` (30 s) and `allowExitOnIdle` so unused connections are closed promptly, keeping memory and socket usage low.\n    -   Added a pool `error` event handler so unexpected errors on idle clients are logged instead of propagating as unhandled exceptions that can corrupt the pool state.\n    -   Added a 30-second hard timeout to every Supabase HTTP request via a custom `fetch` wrapper on the server-side Supabase client. Without this, a slow or temporarily unreachable PostgREST endpoint would cause Supabase queries to hang indefinitely, holding Node.js event-loop resources and contributing to the gradual unresponsiveness over time.\n\n-   Added `isVerbose` option to `CliAgent` so callers can enable the same harness-level console output that `ptbk agent exec --verbose` produces without spawning the CLI. `LiteAgent` already supported `isVerbose`; both classes now expose the option consistently.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat runner not including the agent's initial message (defined via `INITIAL MESSAGE` commitment) in the queued book file when a user sends their first message. The local and external chat runners now prepend the agent's initial message as the opening `MESSAGE @Agent` block so the agent runner sees the full conversation context from the start.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server chat messages being silently cropped when the agent response contained a line starting with a single uppercase ASCII letter followed by lowercase text (e.g. \"V části...\" in Czech). `Book.parse` was incorrectly treating such lines as commitment headers due to an overly permissive regex in `parseCommitmentHeader`. The fix tightens the regex to require at least two characters in the first keyword word, which prevents common natural-language words like \"V\" (Czech for \"in\") or \"A\" / \"I\" in English from being mistaken for commitment markers.\n\n-   Changed Agents Server chat tray ordering from last-activity time to creation time so chats stay in their chronological position and browsing an older chat no longer moves it to the top of the list.\n\n-   Optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server to fix 1–2 fps drops when multiple avatars are visible:\n\n    -   Throttled the shared animation loop to ~24 fps (from the display refresh rate of 60 fps+) via a frame-interval gate in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts`. Animated octopus visuals change slowly enough that 24 fps is perceptually identical to 60 fps while reducing total render work by ~60%.\n    -   Cached stable per-avatar data (morphology profile, animation phase, tentacle profiles, eye phase offsets) using a `WeakMap` keyed on the `createRandom` factory reference in `octopus3dAvatarVisual`, `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`, and `octopus3d3AvatarVisual`. These values are deterministic given the avatar definition and were previously recomputed on every frame.\n    -   Replaced `context.filter = 'blur()'` shadow effects in all six affected visuals (`octopus3d`, `octopus3d2`, `octopus3d3`, `minecraft`, `minecraft2`, `fractal`) with equivalent gradient-based approximations. CSS filter blur forces the browser into a full software rasterization pass on every frame; the gradient alternative is hardware-accelerated and visually equivalent.\n    -   Added `\"ts-node\": { \"transpileOnly\": true }` to `tsconfig.json` so the CLI integration test (`ts-node src/cli/test/ptbk.ts --help`) skips full type-checking during execution. Type correctness is still enforced by the dedicated `test-types` step; this change brings the CLI startup from an uncapped compile pass (> 5 min on Windows) down to ~20 seconds.\n\n-   Further optimized animated avatar rendering performance in Agents Server, building on the earlier 24 fps throttle and stable-state cache. With twelve animated octopus avatars on a single page the previous pass still left the UI at 1–2 fps because every visible avatar fired on the same animation frame and the per-frame mesh sampling cost remained heavy:\n\n    -   Interleaved listeners in `avatarAnimationScheduler.ts` so animated avatars no longer all render on the same animation frame. Each listener now tracks its own last-run timestamp, new listeners are phase-staggered at registration, and the shared loop runs at most `MAX_AVATAR_LISTENERS_PER_FRAME` (= 2) listeners per `requestAnimationFrame`, scheduling the rest on subsequent frames. Each avatar still reaches the 24 fps target individually; total per-frame work is bounded regardless of how many avatars are visible.\n    -   Added per-frame corner-grid sample caching to `octopus3d3AvatarVisual` and `octopus3d2AvatarVisual`. The mesh patch loop previously called `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePoint` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePoint` for each of the four corners of every patch (16×40×4 = 2 560 samples per frame for `octopus3d3`), even though most corners are shared between neighboring patches. The new implementation precomputes a `(latitudePatchCount + 1) × (longitudePatchCount + 1)` corner grid once per frame, cutting the sample call count by ~3.7× on `octopus3d3` and ~4× on `octopus3d2`.\n    -   Added per-frame longitude caching for `resolveContinuousTentacleInfluence`, `resolveContinuousLobeWave`, and `resolveLowerLobeWave` in the same two visuals. Each tentacle-influence evaluation runs an 8-iteration `Math.exp` loop over the seeded tentacle profiles, so calling it once per longitude grid value instead of once per corner cuts the dominant inner-loop cost by ~30×. The new `sampleContinuousOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` / `sampleBlobbyOctopusSurfacePointWithLongitudeCache` helpers accept the cached values explicitly; the existing public sample functions are preserved for off-grid callers (eyes, mouth).\n\n-   Added `--wait [duration]` flag to `ptbk coder run` for controlling the delay between prompt rounds:\n\n    -   `--wait 1h` (or `--wait 30m`, `--wait 5s`, combinations like `--wait 1h30m`) waits the specified duration between rounds to avoid hitting harness rate limits. The first prompt executes immediately; the wait is inserted only before subsequent rounds.\n    -   `--wait` without a value retains the existing interactive behavior — waits for user confirmation before each prompt.\n    -   No flag (or `--no-wait`) means no waiting, which is now the default. `--no-wait` is kept for backward compatibility.\n\n-   Fixed `CliAgent` failing with `Missing --harness in non-dry run mode` when no `harness` is provided: `CliAgent` now falls back to the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable, mirroring `ptbk agent exec` behavior. Similarly falls back to `PTBK_MODEL` and `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL` env vars. Extracted shared env-var constants (`PTBK_HARNESS_ENV`, `PTBK_MODEL_ENV`, `PTBK_THINKING_LEVEL_ENV`), harness names (`CLI_AGENT_HARNESS_NAMES`), and thinking-level values (`CLI_AGENT_THINKING_LEVEL_VALUES`) into the new `src/book-3.0/cliAgentEnv.ts` so CLI and library share a single source of truth. readability and maintainability.\n-   Fix width of the message in the chat by adding a minimum width and improving layout for short messages.\n-   Use model `gemini-3-pro-image-preview` for the agent of Avatar Images\n-   Updated `openai` from `4.63.0` to `6.18.0` and fixed all resulting type errors.\n-   Resolved `zod` peer dependency conflicts between `@ai-sdk/deepseek` and `@openai/agents` by using `overrides` in `package.json`.\n-   Fixed `node-fetch` declaration issue in `LindatAutomaticTranslator.ts` by using native `URLSearchParams` and removing `node-fetch` import.\n-   Stabilized Agents Server under low traffic by removing constant 5-second DB polling from timeout/preparation workers, restoring durable timeout wake-ups through Vercel cron, fixing agent-source cycle detection across canonical/name URLs, and reducing agent-reference resolver churn.\n-   Logged richer durable diagnostics for failed Agents Server chat turns so admin task inspection no longer stops at the generic lease-expired summary:\n\n    -   Added backwards-compatible `failureDetails` storage for `UserChatJob` rows and now persist structured JSON diagnostics containing the failure summary, serialized error payload (message/name/stack when available), provider, timing, and chat-turn identifiers.\n    -   Reused the same diagnostics builder for runtime failures, unexpected worker-route failures, and expired-lease recovery paths to keep failure logging DRY and consistent.\n    -   Extended the admin task manager to surface the stored diagnostics under failed chat-completion tasks via an expandable \"Show details\" panel in the Last error column.\n\n-   Refactored Agents Server `apps/agents-server/src/app/agents/[agentName]/api/chat/route.ts` into smaller focused private chat-route helpers without changing external behavior:\n\n    -   Moved request-time runtime assembly, disclaimer and credential resolution, history initialization, and frozen team-member chat persistence behind the private `resolveAgentChatRouteContext` and `createTeamMemberFrozenChatPersistence` facades so `route.ts` now reads as a thin HTTP entrypoint.\n    -   Extracted the long-lived markdown stream orchestration, cancellation handling, tool-call framing, and final post-processing into the private `createAgentChatStreamResponse` helper while preserving the existing stateless chat streaming behavior, keep-alives, history recording, learning, and calendar activity logging.\n\n-   Enhanced the Agents Server new-agent wizard team step so it now behaves as a homepage-style multi-select picker:\n\n    -   Removed the separate manual \"Team members\" entry UI and kept only the existing-agents picker headed by \"Browse existing agents\" / \"Vyberte existující agenty\".\n    -   Kept multi-selection for teammate agents across the local server and federated servers while continuing to exclude the hidden core server from federated lists.\n    -   Extracted a shared homepage-like `AgentCardsSection` renderer so the wizard and federated-agent surfaces reuse the same card-grid, loading, empty, and error presentation.\n\n-   Improved Agents Server expired chat-worker diagnostics so the stale \"Background worker lease expired before the chat turn finished.\" failure now leaves actionable evidence instead of a generic summary:\n\n    -   Added shared expired-lease diagnostics for durable chat jobs that record queue/run/heartbeat timing, worker runtime thresholds, configured server limits, and a snapshot of active chat jobs and timeouts at the moment recovery runs.\n    -   Started logging structured `lease_expired` recovery/reconciliation events so server logs show which background tasks were active and whether the job had already outlived the 300-second worker route limit when heartbeats stopped.\n\n-   Added immediate optimistic profile-to-chat navigation in Agents Server, so starting a first message from an agent profile now swaps to the chat route without waiting for the server and keeps the user bubble visible throughout the handoff:\n\n    -   Persisted profile-to-chat optimistic turn metadata across the route transition, including the client message id reused later for canonical reconciliation and failure states.\n    -   Added a chat-route loading surface that renders the pending user turn right away while the standalone chat page server data is still loading.\n    -   Tightened optimistic/canonical merge ordering so unresolved user bubbles stay ahead of later assistant streaming messages until the server confirms them.\n\n-   Added the new deterministic `AsciiOctopus` avatar visual alongside the existing avatar set, with an animated ASCII-art rendering that keeps the same organic alien octopus feel as `Octopus3` while varying its blob silhouette, tentacle count, face, and colors from the agent name, hash, colors, and animation time:\n\n    -   Added the new built-in `ascii-octopus` canvas renderer to the shared avatar registry without changing the existing `Octopus`, `Octopus2`, `Octopus3`, pixel-art, Minecraft, or Fractal visuals.\n    -   Kept the implementation DRY by reusing shared octopus body and tentacle geometry helpers, while translating that geometry into deterministic ASCII glyphs instead of painted surfaces.\n    -   Updated the existing utils `/avatars` playground and regression coverage so the new renderer appears in the selector, preview grid, deterministic sample gallery, and supported URL-state parsing without creating a separate page.\n\n-   Fixed Agents Server metadata enum handling so predefined metadata keys no longer accept arbitrary strings in `/admin/metadata`:\n\n    -   Added shared metadata definitions with reusable predefined option lists, so enum-like metadata such as `DEFAULT_AGENT_AVATAR_VISUAL`, `SERVER_LANGUAGE`, `SERVER_VISIBILITY`, `CHAT_FEEDBACK_MODE`, `CHAT_VISUAL_MODE`, `NAME_POOL`, `DEFAULT_VISIBILITY`, and `NEW_AGENT_WIZARD` now render as selects instead of free-form text inputs.\n    -   Reused the same option registries across the metadata page and existing server-creation flows to keep enum values centralized and DRY.\n    -   Added server-side validation for predefined metadata options, so invalid enum values are rejected even when `/api/metadata` is called directly.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk agent-folder run` / `ptbk agent-folder tick` with the GitHub Copilot runner on Windows/MSYS for large queued-message prompts:\n\n    -   Stopped passing the full generated agent prompt as one `copilot -p \"...\"` shell argument, which could exceed the shell/Node argument-length limit and fail with `Argument list too long`.\n    -   Switched the GitHub Copilot runner to feed prompts through standard input instead, keeping `--model`, `--reasoning-effort`, and the existing non-interactive flags unchanged.\n    -   Added regression coverage for the new stdin-based invocation shape so agent-mode prompts stay safe even when the Book Language blueprint makes them much larger than coder prompts.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` rich terminal UI so it now reflects queued-message workflows instead of mirroring `ptbk coder run`:\n\n    -   The top branding now uses compact initials derived from the local `agent.book` title, making the dashboard identify the actual agent definition rather than only the runner selected by `--harness`.\n    -   The session summary now distinguishes the local agent from the execution runner and shows queue-specific totals (`finished` / `queued` / total) with a progress bar based on answered messages instead of `Task 1/1`.\n    -   Added a dedicated `User message` box that shows the latest `MESSAGE @User` block 1:1 with line-preserving trimming, while keeping the live streaming output panel unchanged.\n\n-   Enhanced the `ptbk agent-folder run` terminal dashboard so long-running agent sessions stay inside one stable rich UI:\n\n    -   Kept a single persistent boxed UI alive across queued-message runs, moving idle watching and idle auto-pull activity into explicit in-frame `WAITING` / loading states instead of printing plain lines that broke the layout mid-session.\n    -   Changed the header visual to render the local agent name in a smaller compact banner instead of large initials, while keeping the rest of the terminal frame layout intact.\n    -   Kept the queued-thread preview focused on the latest `MESSAGE @User` from the `.book` thread via `src/book-3.0/Book.ts`, and deferred the coding-agent Git identity tip until process exit so it no longer interrupts active sessions or `--no-ui` streaming output.\n\n-   Refactored `OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools` internals to keep OpenAI Assistants behavior unchanged while making the module easier to follow and maintain:\n\n    -   Split `src/llm-providers/openai/OpenAiAssistantExecutionTools.ts` into a smaller orchestration facade plus focused private helpers for prompt/thread building, tool-run execution, streaming/result reporting, and citation rewriting.\n    -   Kept assistant chat execution, tool progress streaming, hosted tool invocation, file attachment handling, assistant creation/update flows, and final Promptbook result export behavior unchanged while reducing the responsibility count inside the top-level file.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server of Agents Server, which rejected every management call and therefore never routed inbound or outbound agent mail:\n\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which decided that Stalwart was already bootstrapped whenever `/etc/stalwart/config.json` existed. Stalwart writes that file itself - it is only its storage descriptor, for example `{\"@type\":\"RocksDb\",\"path\":\"/var/lib/stalwart/\",...}` - already during its very first startup, long before anything is bootstrapped, and never touches it again. The installer therefore skipped the `x:Bootstrap/set` call on **every** fresh installation and left the mail server permanently in bootstrap mode, where it refuses every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`. The bootstrap state is now read from Stalwart itself through a management probe, so a pending bootstrap is completed on the next installer run and an already bootstrapped server is left untouched.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart management payloads, which sent JSON arrays for `aliases`, `credentials`, `memberGroupIds`, `stages`, and the MTA hook `enable.match` expression, while Stalwart serializes every `set` / `objectList` property as an object and answered `invalidPatch` / `Invalid value for object property`. Added shared `toStalwartJmapSet` and `toStalwartJmapObjectList` helpers so all payloads build these shapes in one place.\n    -   Fixed `install.sh`, which provisioned the Agents Server Stalwart administrator inside the reserved `promptbook.invalid` domain. Stalwart rejects such a domain as an `Invalid domain name`, so the step failed and, because of `set -Eeuo pipefail`, aborted the whole installation before nginx, firewall, and certificate configuration ever ran. The bootstrap-time administrator credentials are now kept as Stalwart's fixed `STALWART_RECOVERY_ADMIN` credentials instead of provisioning a second administrator account.\n    -   Fixed the Stalwart step of `install.sh` aborting the whole installation when the mail server cannot be bootstrapped. Because `configure_firewall`, `configure_nginx_reverse_proxy`, and `configure_ssl_certificates` all run afterwards, a mail server problem used to leave the VPS without a firewall, reverse proxy, or certificates. The step now warns and continues, and the bootstrap is retried by every later installer run.\n    -   Fixed outbound submission, which was configured for port `587`, a port a bootstrapped Stalwart never opens. Agents Server now submits through `submissions` on port `465` with implicit TLS, and the email server administration pages document that port instead of `587`.\n    -   Fixed the catch-all address being assigned before the mailbox behind it existed, so synchronizing an already-known domain no longer fails on its first management call.\n    -   Improved Stalwart error reporting so a rejected object now includes Stalwart's own `notCreated` / `notUpdated` reason, and a server still in **bootstrap mode** reports an actionable message instead of a raw `forbidden` response.\n    -   Fixed the `promptbook-agents-server` build, which loaded the Next.js command line interface through the hardcoded path `../../node_modules/next/dist/bin/next`. That path does not exist inside a git worktree without its own installed dependencies, such as the `ptbk coder --isolate` worktrees, so `npm run build` failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` even though Next.js was resolvable. The new `apps/agents-server/scripts/next-cli.js` resolves it through Node's own module resolution instead.\n\n-   Fixed the self-contained Stalwart mail server staying unusable whenever its initial setup was left pending. Completing that setup used to be the sole responsibility of `install.sh`, so a mail server which was installed before the bootstrap fix - or whose bootstrap failed once - answered every management call with `{\"type\":\"forbidden\",\"description\":\"The server is in bootstrap mode. ...\"}`, and **Synchronize Stalwart** on `/admin/email-server` could only report the error, never resolve it. Because the VPS self-update runs the _deployed_ release's installer, such a server stayed broken for at least one more update cycle. Agents Server now completes the bootstrap itself as the first step of every domain synchronization, which happens on startup and on **Synchronize Stalwart**, and it asks Stalwart for its bootstrap state instead of inferring it from files on disk. The setup Stalwart receives - mail hostname, default domain, automatic DKIM keys, and no ACME certificate request because nginx and certbot own every certificate on the VPS - is now defined by `buildStalwartBootstrapValue`, which `install.sh` mirrors under the shared `[📬]` marker because a fresh VPS is bootstrapped before Agents Server is built, and the result is verified against Stalwart itself so a bootstrap that was accepted but not applied is reported with the remaining manual step instead of a raw `forbidden` response. The installer keeps performing the bootstrap for a fresh installation and additionally waits until Stalwart really left bootstrap mode after the restart it needs to open its mail listeners, so the first synchronization of a newly started Agents Server no longer races a mail server that is still coming up.\n-   Improved the Agents Server **Book language manual** so its linked table of contents navigates directly to each commitment, and each end-to-end example links its used commitments back to their sections. The manual now describes `@Foo` and `{Foo foo}` as agent references rather than parameters, renames the `---` primitive to **Multiple agent**, documents code fences as ` ``` `, links every generated-from source to the Promptbook repository, hides parser/runtime implementation details and unfinished commitments, and keeps each commitment example focused on its canonical keyword with only `GOAL` and `CLOSED` as supporting syntax.\n\n-   Fixed the published `@promptbook/components` package, which broke the production build of every browser application that installs `ptbk`, `promptbook` or `@promptbook/components`. Rendered markdown is sanitized by `DOMPurify`, which needs a DOM, so `renderMarkdown` creates one through `jsdom` whenever it runs outside of a browser - for example during server-side rendering. That code path is unreachable in a browser, but bundlers resolve `require('jsdom')` statically, so `next build` followed it into `jsdom` and failed with **Module not found: Can't resolve `fs`** together with the same error for `child_process` and `net`. It failed even for an application that imports `<MarkdownContent/>` with `ssr: false`, because a bundler resolves a module it will never execute just as eagerly as one it will:\n\n    -   The generated manifest of every package that is not Node-only now declares `\"browser\": { \"jsdom\": false }`, which is the standard way to tell a browser bundler to replace a Node-only dependency with an empty module. Browser builds therefore no longer follow `jsdom` (and no longer ship it), while Node.js ignores the `browser` field and keeps resolving the real library for server-side rendering. The stubs are derived from the dependencies which the generated package really has, so a Node-only dependency which appears in a browser-facing package in the future is covered without another manual change.\n    -   Creating the server-side DOM moved from `renderMarkdown` into `$provideServerDomWindow`, which is now the single place where browser-facing code touches `jsdom`. A runtime that can provide neither the DOM of a browser nor `jsdom` is now reported as a branded `EnvironmentMismatchError` explaining why markdown can not be sanitized, instead of failing with `JSDOM is not a constructor`.\n    -   The list of Node-only packages is now shared through `isNodeOnlyPackage` between the publish-safety check and the dependency step of the package generation, instead of being written down twice.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":20,"lines":["+-   A generated system message no longer repeats the same instructions. Commitments are applied one by one, so a","+    commitment used several times in one book emitted its whole section every time, including the shared guidance","+    paragraph which introduces it. Two `WRITING RULES` blocks produced two `## Writing rules` headings each preceded by","+    the same four-line explanation of what a writing rule is, two `USE PRIVACY` blocks produced the `## Privacy`","+    instructions twice, and the same held for `WRITING SAMPLE`, `SAMPLE`, `LANGUAGE`, `USE POPUP`,","+    `USE IMAGE GENERATOR`, `USE USER LOCATION` and `TEAM`. The final system message is now deduplicated once for all","+    commitments instead of being fixed in each of them separately:","+","+    -   All sections sharing one `## Title` are merged into the position of their first occurrence, so each heading","+        appears exactly once while the content of every commitment keeps its original order inside that section.","+    -   Every identical block is kept only once, so the shared guidance paragraph of a repeated commitment is stated","+        once and a repeated instruction without its own heading, such as `STYLE Formal.` written twice, is no longer","+        duplicated.","+    -   Merged bullet lists stay one compact list, and fenced code blocks - imported files and inline `KNOWLEDGE`","+        content among them - are never split or deduplicated.","+    -   Commitments written once produce exactly the same system message as before.","+"," -   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and","     thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now","     names the agent which implemented it:"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false}}

}\n\n    return splitSystemMessageIntoRegions(systemMessage)\n        .reduce(mergeRegionSharingHeading, [])\n        .map(removeDuplicateBlocksFromRegion)\n        .map(renderRegion)\n `createRegion`\n */\nfunction splitBodyIntoBlocks(bodyLines: ReadonlyArray<string>): ReadonlyArray<string> {\n    const blocks: string[] = [];\n    let blockLines: string[] = [];\n    let {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XzUJXjWAZ2FuZXJJ7ygWvK","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /Users/hejny/work/promptbook/changelog/_current-preversion.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"bff3bbec-f916-44e2-9b1b-3a9effb2c4a0","uuid":"50c25546-a1ae-4659-bce6-57becbcebed9","timestamp":"2026-09-14T18:23:02.565Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"/Users/hejny/work/promptbook/changelog/_current-preversion.md","oldString":"    -   Merged bullet lists stay one compact list, and fenced code blocks - imported files and inline `KNOWLEDGE`\n        content among them - are never split or deduplicated.\n    -   Commitments written once produce exactly the same system message as before.","newString":"    -   Two lists joined by a merge become one compact list, while everything which was not merged keeps its original\n        spacing, and fenced code blocks - imported files and inline `KNOWLEDGE` content among them - are never split\n        or deduplicated.\n    -   A book which uses each of its commitments once produces the same system message as before.","originalFile":"-   A generated system message no longer repeats the same instructions. Commitments are applied one by one, so a\n    commitment used several times in one book emitted its whole section every time, including the shared guidance\n    paragraph which introduces it. Two `WRITING RULES` blocks produced two `## Writing rules` headings each preceded by\n    the same four-line explanation of what a writing rule is, two `USE PRIVACY` blocks produced the `## Privacy`\n    instructions twice, and the same held for `WRITING SAMPLE`, `SAMPLE`, `LANGUAGE`, `USE POPUP`,\n    `USE IMAGE GENERATOR`, `USE USER LOCATION` and `TEAM`. The final system message is now deduplicated once for all\n    commitments instead of being fixed in each of them separately:\n\n    -   All sections sharing one `## Title` are merged into the position of their first occurrence, so each heading\n        appears exactly once while the content of every commitment keeps its original order inside that section.\n    -   Every identical block is kept only once, so the shared guidance paragraph of a repeated commitment is stated\n        once and a repeated instruction without its own heading, such as `STYLE Formal.` written twice, is no longer\n        duplicated.\n    -   Merged bullet lists stay one compact list, and fenced code blocks - imported files and inline `KNOWLEDGE`\n        content among them - are never split or deduplicated.\n    -   Commitments written once produce exactly the same system message as before.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now tracks the agent of a run next to its harness and model. Two runs of the same harness, model and\n    thinking level are not the same run when one of them carries an `--agent`, so the run report of every prompt now\n    names the agent which implemented it:\n\n    -   A prompt status line signs its work with the agent in front of the harness, as\n        `` [x] by Developer on OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max` (ChatGPT account) - Implementation ~$0.13 23 minutes ``.\n        The `[^]`, `[x]` and `[!]` status lines and the run trace of the round all report it, and a prompt continued\n        through `--git-changes continue` keeps the agent in each of its chronological `interrupted, continued by …`\n        reports.\n    -   The reported name is the display name of the Book — its `META FULLNAME`, or the plain title on its first line\n        — so `agents/coding/developer.book` signs as its Book title and not as its normalized identifier.\n    -   A run started without `--agent` reports exactly what it reported before.\n\n-   Fixed `MockedChat` typing animations blinking for messages without ids by assigning stable playback-only ids before rendering each simulated transcript.\n\n-   Fixed the rich `ptbk coder run` dashboard so an animated agent avatar can no longer overwrite its own UI in an\n    exact-width terminal pane:\n\n    -   The shared frame layout now leaves one physical terminal column unused, preventing boxed rows from\n        auto-wrapping and keeping incremental cursor-based redraws aligned with their logical frame rows.\n    -   Added a focused VS Code terminal preset and regression coverage for the terminal-width invariant.\n\n-   Added agent-specific prompt routing to `ptbk coder`:\n\n    -   A ready `[ ]` prompt can now target the Book passed in `--agent` with a backtick-delimited path, filename,\n        filename without `.book`, or the Book title from its first line. For example, a run using\n        `--agent agents/coding/developer.book` accepts `agents/coding/developer.book`, `developer.book`,\n        `developer`, and `Promptbook Developer` routing tokens.\n    -   Agent references work alongside the existing model and harness routing tokens, and `ptbk coder list --agent\n        <path.book>` previews the same agent-specific queue without starting a harness.\n    -   Added an Unslopper agent preset next to the developer preset in the local VS Code terminal scripts and\n        documented agent-specific routing on the `ptbk coder` landing page.\n\n-   The help of `ptbk` does not advertise the deprecated commands anymore. `run`, `login`, `make`, `prettify`, `test`,\n    `list-models`, `list-scrapers`, `start-agents-server` and `start-pipelines-server` are all leftovers of the old\n    pipeline system, yet nine of the fifteen commands which `ptbk --help` listed were exactly those, each one with its\n    own `Deprecated:` paragraph, so the listing which is supposed to introduce the CLI was mostly made of commands\n    nobody should start using. `ptbk --help`, and the same listing which plain `ptbk` prints when it asks for a\n    subcommand, now offers only the commands which are meant to be used - `coder`, `agent`, `agent-folder`,\n    `agents-server`, `about` and `hello`. Nothing was removed: every deprecated command still runs, still warns that it\n    is deprecated when it is used, still explains the deprecation in its own help - `ptbk run --help` - and is still\n    reachable through `ptbk help run`. Only the \"did you mean\" hint for a mistyped command stops pointing at them.\n    Being left out of the help is now simply a part of what deprecating a command means, written once in\n    `$deprecateCliCommand`, so any command deprecated later disappears from the help on its own.\n\n-   `ptbk` without a subcommand no longer falls back to the deprecated `ptbk run`. Until now `run` was registered as\n    the default command of the CLI, so everything which did not name a command - `ptbk ./write-cv.book`, a mistyped\n    `ptbk codr` or a stray option - was quietly handed over to the pipeline runner of the old system, which was the\n    last thing a deprecated command should be doing. Plain `ptbk` now asks to specify a subcommand and prints the\n    top-level help, exactly like `ptbk coder`, `ptbk agent`, `ptbk agent-folder` and `ptbk agents-server` already did\n    when they were called without one of their own subcommands, and that one shared behavior is now written once\n    instead of five times. Anything which is not a command is refused with `unknown command` and a \"did you mean\"\n    hint instead of being executed as a pipeline, so a script which still passes a book path to `ptbk` fails loudly\n    rather than appearing to succeed. `ptbk run` itself is untouched and keeps working for everyone who asks for it\n    explicitly. The command list in the help now starts with `coder`, followed by `agent`, `agent-folder` and\n    `agents-server`, and the deprecated commands of the old pipeline system are listed after them.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` now saves the run trace of every prompt round, so a finished run can still be analyzed afterwards.\n    Until now the only durable record of a round was the one status line written into the prompt file: the live\n    runtime log holding everything the harness and the verification command had written was a temporary artifact,\n    deleted as soon as a successful round was over unless `--preserve-logs` was passed, and lost together with the\n    reasoning, the tool calls and the diffs of the run. Each round now writes `prompts/traces/<prompt-file-name>.md`\n    - a trace named exactly like the prompt file it belongs to, with the same `-2` section suffix the temporary\n    scripts of a multi-section prompt file already use. The trace pairs the metadata of the round - which prompt and\n    section it implemented, whether it succeeded or failed, the harness, model, thinking level and login method which\n    ran it, how many coding attempts it took, what each step cost and how long each one ran, the verification\n    command, the start, end and duration, and the error which ended a failed round - with the untouched runtime log\n    of the harness. Because the trace is written before the round is committed, it lands in the very same commit as\n    the prompt it describes, and a task whose isolated worktree cannot be merged back carries its trace into the\n    failure commit instead. A failed round is traced too, next to the `.error.log` it already wrote. Re-running the\n    same prompt overwrites its trace and leaves the earlier ones in the git history.\n\n-   `ptbk coder run` and `ptbk coder server` no longer walk into a full disk. A coding round writes prompt and log\n    artifacts, lets the harness rewrite the project, may install npm packages, may create a git worktree for\n    `--isolate` and usually runs a build, so a run started without enough space used to die somewhere in the middle,\n    after the coding agent had already rewritten a part of the project. The free disk space is now measured before\n    anything is installed or written: with less than 2 GB left the command refuses to start and says how much space\n    is left, how much is needed and how to get it back, instead of failing later with a raw filesystem error. The\n    same measurement is repeated while the run is in progress - at the checkpoints where `ptbk coder` can stop\n    anyway, so it is checked before every round, every verification and every commit - and once less than 1 GB is\n    left the run reports the same warning and pauses there, waiting for the disk space to be freed and for `P` to\n    resume it. The limit to keep running is lower than the limit to start, because interrupting a round which is\n    already in progress costs more than not starting one. A run started with `--no-questions` never pauses, because\n    there is nobody who could free the disk space and resume it - it reports the warning and keeps going. A platform\n    which cannot report its free disk space never stops a run.\n\n-   Added `--no-questions` to every `ptbk coder` command which can stop and wait for an answer it does not strictly\n    need. `init`, `add`, `run`, `ping` and `server` still do all their work, but no longer ask anything: installing\n    a missing coding harness, updating an outdated one, updating an outdated Promptbook CLI and adding the missing\n    harness ignore rules to `.gitignore` are all skipped and reported together with the command which does them\n    manually, and `ptbk coder add` refuses a missing description instead of asking for it. Because an outdated\n    harness or CLI can only be updated after a confirmation, `--no-questions` also skips the npm latest-version\n    lookup which would only lead to a question, which is what the never released `--no-harness-update` used to do -\n    that flag is replaced by `--no-questions` and is gone. The one combination which can not work,\n    `--no-auto --no-questions`, is refused right away instead of waiting forever for a confirmation nobody may be\n    asked for. `ptbk coder verify` does not take the flag, because walking through finished prompts and asking about\n    each of them is the only thing it does.\n\n-   `ptbk coder` no longer answers a harness which is not logged in with a wall of raw CLI output. A harness whose\n    login is missing or whose session has expired now fails with a short branded `AuthenticationError` which names\n    the harness, quotes the one sentence the harness itself reported - such as `Failed to authenticate: OAuth session\n    expired and could not be refreshed` - and says exactly how to sign in again, for example by running `claude` and\n    then the `/login` command inside it. How each harness is signed in is described once, next to how it is installed\n    and detected, and the failure is recognized once for every harness and for every command\n    which runs prompts, so `coder run`, `coder server` and `coder ping` all report it the same way. The terminal and\n    the `.error.log` file written next to the prompt both show those instructions on their own now, instead of\n    following them with a stack trace of a failure nobody can debug. Because no retry of a harness which is not\n    logged in can ever succeed, such a prompt is also no longer retried three times with the `--wait-after-error`\n    delay in between - the instructions are shown right away.\n\n-   Fixed the wall of `npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings printed when installing `ptbk`:\n\n    -   The Vercel AI SDK providers `@ai-sdk/openai`, `@ai-sdk/google` and `@ai-sdk/deepseek` were still on the\n        generation which accepts only Zod 3, while the rest of the ecosystem - the Agents Server, `@openai/agents`,\n        `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` - needs Zod 4. No single Zod could satisfy both sides, so npm reported a conflict\n        for every one of those packages. They are upgraded to the newest generation which accepts both Zod 3 and\n        Zod 4 and still runs on Node.js 18, so the supported Node.js versions of Promptbook do not change, and\n        `createExecutionToolsFromVercelProvider` is migrated to the model interface of that generation. Settings\n        given as `additionalChatSettings` are now passed to the model call instead of to the model constructor,\n        which is where the Vercel AI SDK expects them, and the `userId` option is no longer sent as the `user`\n        setting, because it has become specific to each provider.\n    -   Generated packages no longer publish dependencies which only look like imports. Package generation infers\n        dependencies by reading the generated bundle, and it used to count module specifiers written inside the\n        source-code templates of the transpilers, so `@promptbook/core` published `zod`, `dotenv` and\n        `@anthropic-ai/sdk` as runtime dependencies although it never imports any of them. The pinned `zod` in\n        particular forced one exact Zod version onto every project which installs Promptbook.\n    -   Generated packages no longer carry the `overrides` field of the repository. npm honors overrides only in the\n        root project of an installation, so publishing them only left a dangling reference to a dependency which the\n        published package does not declare.\n\n    What remains after this are three warnings about React 19 coming from packages inside `swagger-ui-react`, which\n    are declared by projects outside of Promptbook.\n\n-   The hero headline of the **ptbk coder** landing page now rotates through seven claims instead of saying one\n    thing forever. Every claim is written once in a single configuration the rotating headline, the page tagline\n    and the sharing image all read, and the claims crossfade with a slight vertical slide - the claim which leaves\n    rises out of the headline while the next one rises into it. All claims share one grid cell, so the headline\n    keeps the height of the tallest of them and nothing around it moves while they rotate. The same reserved\n    height finally balances the hero: together with a terminal text size tuned one step down, the copy column now\n    reaches almost as high as the live terminal next to it, instead of floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defines. Visitors whose system prefers reduced motion keep the first claim without rotation.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` overwriting configuration the project already owns. Existing `package.json` scripts and\n    `.vscode/settings.json` settings are now kept verbatim and only genuinely missing ones are added. Files a default\n    script points at, like `agents/developer.book`, `AGENTS.md` and `prompts/templates/common.md`, are created only\n    together with the script which references them, so a project with its own `coder:run` no longer receives an unused\n    default agent. `ptbk coder init` also initializes the `test-for-ptbk-coder` npm script which the default\n    `coder:run` uses as its verification command.\n\n-   Rebalanced the hero of the **ptbk coder** landing page, whose live terminal used to be much taller than the copy\n    next to it and left the headline, the install command and the buttons floating in the middle of a section the\n    terminal alone defined:\n\n    -   The terminal window is now never wider than the character grid it draws, so a layout with more width than the\n        widest supported terminal - a tablet, a phone in landscape - gets a centered window instead of a window with an\n        empty half, and it fills the height of the copy column whenever the copy is the taller one.\n    -   A terminal row is now as tight as a real terminal emulator draws it, which both shortens the sample session by\n        about one tenth and keeps the frames of the dashboard boxes connected.\n    -   The box drawing characters, the shade of the progress bar and the status marks are missing from the latin\n        subset of the terminal font, so they were drawn from the fallback which `next/font` derives from a\n        **proportional** font - about one and a half character cells wide and shorter than one row, which broke every\n        box border of the dashboard into detached segments. The terminal font now falls back to the monospace fonts of\n        the system, so those characters are drawn one cell wide and one row tall and the boxes are drawn as continuous\n        frames.\n    -   The hero copy is now read at hero size: the headline and the subheadline grow with the viewport, but only as\n        far as their own column can carry them, so the headline keeps its two lines from the narrowest phone to the\n        widest desktop.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` so it no longer creates an `AGENT_CODING.md` quick-reference file.\n-   Redesigned the three core benefit illustrations on the **ptbk coder** landing page with detailed terminal,\n    portable-agent, and synchronized-commit scenes, plus proportional graphics and a more readable tablet layout.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder init` to preserve a non-empty `prompts/` directory instead of adding placeholder boilerplate\n    prompts while it initializes the remaining coder files.\n\n-   Added `ptbk coder list`, a read-only queue preview that lists ready, fully authored prompts in descending priority\n    groups without starting a harness. Its optional `--harness`, `--model`, `--priority`, `--min-priority`, and\n    `--max-priority` filters let you preview exactly the queue a selected runner would receive.\n\n-   Added a live GitHub star counter and **Star on GitHub** call to action to the **ptbk coder** landing page.\n\n-   Added support for plain markdown prompts without a status checkbox in **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder run` and\n    `ptbk coder server` now treat them as ready prompts at priority `0`, then insert the normal live `[^]` status line\n    before their content as processing begins and finish them through the usual `[x]` or `[!]` flow.\n\n-   Added queue opt-out markers to **ptbk coder**. `[.]` now behaves like `[-]`, keeping that prompt out of the queue,\n    and `<!--ptbk-coder-ignore-->` anywhere in a Markdown prompt file excludes the entire file from `run`, `list`, and\n    `server`.\n\n-   Added project-local harness ignore rules to **ptbk coder**. `ptbk coder init` now adds the rules for every supported\n    harness, including `.qwen`; `ptbk coder run`, `ptbk coder server`, and `ptbk coder ping` detect a missing selected\n    harness rule and use the same interactive `[y/N]` confirmation as harness installation updates before adding it.\n\n-   Fixed globally installing `ptbk` on Node.js 26, including macOS arm64. `ptbk coder` can now be installed without\n    `better-sqlite3` 11 falling back to a native build against removed V8 APIs; the generated CLI now receives\n    `better-sqlite3` 12.11.1, which supplies the matching Node 26 binary.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server production build failing when its Edge middleware reached standalone SQLite code.\n    SQLite registry loading now lives in a Node.js-only module, and custom-domain routing reads its needed federation\n    settings through the middleware's supplied Supabase client. Edge middleware can therefore route configured domains\n    without compiling `better-sqlite3` into its bundle.\n\n-   Fixed `ptbk coder --harness openai-codex --model default` failing for everyone signed in to OpenAI Codex with a\n    ChatGPT account. `default` silently stood for `gpt-5.2-codex`, which such an account rejects with\n    _\"The 'gpt-5.2-codex' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account\"_ — so both\n    `ptbk coder ping` and `ptbk coder run` died before doing any work.\n\n    -   `--model default` now overrides **no model at all** for OpenAI Codex: Codex is started without `--model` and\n        keeps the model from its own configuration _(`~/.codex/config.toml`)_, exactly like `--model default` already\n        worked for GitHub Copilot. Whatever a ChatGPT-account login is allowed to use therefore works.\n    -   Naming a model explicitly, for example `--model gpt-5.2-codex`, is unchanged, and `--model` is still required\n        for OpenAI Codex.\n    -   For `gemini` and `qwen-code`, `default` keeps standing for their concrete default model, because those CLIs\n        have no configured default to fall back to.\n    -   When Codex picks the model itself, the reported price is estimated from the fallback pricing, because only\n        Codex knows which model it really used.\n\n-   Fixed **ptbk coder** updating a coding harness with `npm install -g` even when npm does not own that harness. A\n    Codex installed by the official standalone installer was reported as outdated and \"updated\" into a _second_ Codex\n    inside the active Node prefix, while the Codex which actually runs stayed on its old version — and which of the two\n    was used from then on depended on the active Node version.\n\n    -   Before offering an update, `ptbk coder` now resolves which file the harness command really executes _(following\n        symbolic links, using the very same `PATH` which runs the harness)_ and recognizes whether it belongs to a\n        global npm installation, a standalone installation, or Homebrew.\n    -   A **standalone installation is updated with its own updater** — `codex update` for OpenAI Codex — and a\n        **Homebrew installation is never touched**, only `brew upgrade …` is printed. When the harness command cannot\n        be traced to any of these, `ptbk coder` says so and leaves it alone instead of guessing, because\n        `npm install -g` would install a second copy next to it.\n    -   The outdated-harness warning now also prints the resolved command path and how it was installed, and the\n        confirmation question names the exact command which is about to run, so an update can no longer be approved\n        without knowing what it does.\n    -   Installing a harness which is missing altogether is unchanged: it is still installed globally through npm.\n\n-   Added the singular `WRITING RULE` keyword as an equivalent variant of `WRITING RULES`, exactly like `RULE` and\n    `RULES` are interchangeable. Both spellings are parsed, applied, documented, and syntax-highlighted identically, so\n    a single writing constraint no longer has to be written in plural.\n\n-   Fixed the Agents Server starting one more pm2 process of the same agent project on every single start, which\n    eventually took the whole server down.\n\n    -   Every project runtime is registered under a stable pm2 process name, and a project was expected to be replaced\n        rather than duplicated because it is deleted right before it is started again. That delete was **skipped\n        whenever pm2 could not be asked for its process list**, and `pm2 start` appends a second process instead of\n        refusing a name it already knows, so each start added one more copy of the same project.\n    -   The process list could not be read because `pm2 jlist` embeds a full environment snapshot into every listed\n        process — roughly 70 kB each — while its output was capped at one megabyte. A dozen projects were enough to\n        exceed that cap, after which **every** pm2 query failed with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` and reported\n        every process as unknown. Each new duplicate made the output larger, so the failure never recovered on its own.\n    -   Every duplicate got its own port but the project's dev command kept binding the port it had chosen itself, so\n        all but one copy crash-looped on `EADDRINUSE`, and pm2 restarted them hundreds of times per hour until the VPS\n        ran out of threads (`pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable`) and the Agents Server itself was\n        killed.\n    -   Deleting a project process no longer depends on reading the process list: it is always attempted, only pm2\n        itself reporting an unknown name counts as \"already gone\", and any other failure is reported instead of\n        swallowed — so a project is now left alone rather than duplicated when pm2 misbehaves. Because `pm2 delete`\n        removes every process sharing one name, a server which already accumulated duplicates converges back to a\n        single process per project.\n\n-   Added the **Qwen Code** harness, so `ptbk coder` now drives seven coding agents instead of six.\n\n    -   `ptbk coder run --harness qwen-code --model qwen3.8-max` runs the whole prompt queue through the Qwen Code CLI,\n        and every other harness-aware command — `ptbk coder ping`, `ptbk coder server`, `ptbk agent exec`, `CliAgent`\n        and the `PTBK_HARNESS` environment variable — accepts `qwen-code` the same way.\n    -   Like `openai-codex` and `gemini`, Qwen Code **requires an explicit `--model`**; `--model default` resolves to\n        `qwen3.8-max`. Its global `@qwen-code/qwen-code` installation is checked and updated before the first prompt,\n        just like the other harnesses. Qwen Code exposes no reasoning-effort flag, so `--thinking-level` does not\n        apply to it.\n    -   Price estimation of harnesses which do not report their own token counts is now shared between Qwen Code and\n        Gemini instead of being written twice.\n\n-   Fixed generated `ptbk` prompt emoji tags so `coder add`, `coder generate-boilerplates`, refactor prompt generation, and `coder find-fresh-emoji-tags` share one Unicode-valid single-pictogram catalogue instead of a duplicated legacy list containing non-emoji symbols. The emoji-tag scan cache now records the candidate catalogue fingerprint and rescans when it changes, so an already assigned tag such as `[✨🛼]` is not mistaken for a fresh tag after an update.\n\n-   Added remaining subscription-limit visibility to the rich **ptbk coder** terminal dashboard.\n\n    -   The `Session` box now lists every rolling limit a selected harness reports, including its remaining percentage\n        and reset time. It does not assume a fixed pair of windows, so a 5-hour, weekly, model-specific, or future\n        additional limit all render as separate aligned rows.\n    -   OpenAI Codex reads its current account snapshot through the Codex app-server protocol, while Claude Code\n        reuses its normal `stream-json` rate-limit events instead of spending a separate quota-only prompt. Other\n        harnesses keep their existing behavior until they implement the same optional runner capability.\n    -   Updated the **ptbk coder** landing-page terminal demo and pacing copy to show the new 5-hour and 7-day\n        subscription rows.\n\n-   Let you decide what **ptbk coder** does with a dirty working tree. The clean-working-tree guard used to be a yes/no\n    question — either the coder refused to start, or `--ignore-git-changes` waved the changes through. The far more\n    common case had no answer at all: a run that was killed or crashed mid-task, leaving half-finished work in the tree\n    and one prompt stuck in the in-progress `[^]` status. The only way forward was to throw that work away.\n\n    -   **The new `--git-changes <fail|ignore|continue>` replaces `--ignore-git-changes`**, which is gone; use\n        `--git-changes ignore` instead. `fail` stays the default and now says in its error which of the other two modes\n        to reach for.\n    -   **`--git-changes continue` resumes the interrupted prompt** with its uncommitted changes still in place. It\n        expects **exactly one** prompt in the `[^]` status and refuses to guess otherwise: finding none or finding\n        several fails with a message naming the prompts it found, because the changes in the tree cannot be attributed\n        to a single task. Only that one round runs on the dirty tree — once it is committed, every later round expects a\n        clean working tree again. It cannot be combined with `--isolate`, whose fresh worktree is checked out from the\n        last commit and would leave exactly those changes behind, or `--test-before yes-and-fix`, which has no\n        unmodified project state to verify and repair.\n    -   **A prompt one harness started and another one finished says so in chronological order.** A resumed status\n        now reads `` [^] by OpenAI Codex `gpt-5.6-luna` thinking `max`, interrupted, continued by Claude Code `claude-opus-5` thinking `high` - Implementation in progress ``,\n        and the `[x]` and `[!]` lines keep that report. Each further `--git-changes continue` invocation extends the\n        same report with another `interrupted, continued by …` segment, so no earlier harness is dropped; resuming the\n        same harness keeps its existing authentication label instead of naming it twice. The live status still reports\n        its active phase, but the final continuation report omits its partial step usage and duration rather than\n        presenting them as the whole task. All three statuses go through one\n        [`formatPromptRunnerAttribution`](../scripts/run-codex-prompts/prompts/promptRunnerAttribution.ts), which also\n        understands the reverse-ordered `started by` status lines written by the preceding version.\n    -   `ptbk coder server` and `ptbk agent-folder run` share the same flag. An agent folder answers queued messages\n        instead of running a prompt queue, so `continue` keeps the changes there exactly like `ignore` does.\n\n-   Made the terminal controls of **ptbk coder** answer every key press. Pressing `P`, `S` or `X` used to be a leap of\n    faith: `S Skip current waiting` in particular changed nothing on screen, so there was no way to tell whether the key\n    had arrived, whether the wait was being skipped, or whether the terminal had simply stopped repainting.\n\n    -   **Every press is now answered inside the `Controls` box**, on the frame that follows it, for example\n        `» S Skipping the current waiting, continuing right now`. A press which changes nothing is answered too\n        (`» S Nothing to skip, the coder is not waiting right now`), because \"nothing happened\" and \"the key was lost\"\n        must not look the same.
